sentences.zh: 蘇味道

translations.literal: Su Weidao
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao

sentences.zh: 蘇味道，趙州欒城人也。

translations.literal: Su Weidao was a native of Luancheng in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao came from Luancheng in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 少與鄉人李嶠俱以文辭知名，時人謂之蘇李。

translations.literal: In youth he and his fellow townsman Li Jiao were both famous for literary composition; people of the time called them Su and Li.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he and his fellow townsman Li Jiao were both known for their literary talent, and people of the day called them "Su and Li."

sentences.zh: 弱冠，本州舉進士。

translations.literal: At twenty he was recommended as a jinshi graduate by his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was nominated as a jinshi graduate by his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累轉咸陽尉。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he became assistant magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to assistant magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎裴行儉先知其貴，甚加禮遇，及征突厥阿史那都支，引為管記。

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, foresaw his future eminence and treated him with great courtesy; when he campaigned against the Turk Ashina Duzhi, he took Weidao on as staff recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, had early recognized his promise and treated him with great respect; when Pei campaigned against the Turk Ashina Duzhi, he took Weidao on as staff recorder.

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝妃父裴居道再登左金吾將軍，訪當時才子為謝表，托於味道，援筆而成，辭理精密，盛傳於代。

translations.literal: Pei Judao, father of the consort of Emperor Xiaojing, was again appointed general of the Left Golden Crow Guard; he sought out a leading literary talent of the day to compose a memorial of thanks and entrusted it to Weidao, who took up the brush and finished it at once—its language and reasoning were precise and it was widely celebrated in the generation.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Judao, father of the consort of Emperor Xiaojing, was again appointed general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, he looked for a leading literary talent of the day to draft a memorial of thanks and entrusted the task to Weidao. Weidao took up his brush and finished it at once; the prose was precise in argument and eloquence, and it was widely celebrated in his generation.

sentences.zh: 延載初，曆遷鳳閣舍人、檢校鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，尋加正授，證聖元年，坐事，出為集州刺史，俄召拜天官侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai he was promoted through the posts of secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion, acting secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion, and co-signatory of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace affairs; soon afterward he received full appointment. In the first year of Zhengsheng, for an offense he was sent out as prefect of Jizhou, but was soon recalled and appointed vice minister of the heaven office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanzai era he rose through the posts of secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion, acting secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion, and co-signatory of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace affairs, and soon received full appointment. In the first year of Zhengsheng he was dismissed for an offense and sent out as prefect of Jizhou, but was soon recalled and appointed vice minister of the heaven office.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，遷鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenli he was transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion and made associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenli he was transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion and appointed associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 味道善敷奏，多識台閣故事，然而前後居相位數載，竟不能有所發明，但脂韋其間，苟度取容而已。

translations.literal: Weidao was skilled at presenting memorials and knew many precedents of the central administration; yet over several years in the chief ministership he accomplished nothing of note, merely greasing his way through office and seeking only to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao was adept at presenting memorials and knew many precedents of the central administration, yet during several years as chief minister he never accomplished anything of note—he only greased his way through office and sought nothing beyond keeping himself in favor.

sentences.zh: 嚐謂人曰“處事不欲決斷明白，若有錯誤，必貽咎譴，但模棱以持兩端可矣。”

translations.literal: He once told others, "In handling affairs one should not wish to decide clearly; if there is error, reproach and punishment will surely follow—it is enough merely to be equivocal and hold both sides."
translations.idiomatic: He once said to others, "In handling affairs one should not strive to decide clearly. If one is wrong, reproach and punishment will surely follow—it is enough simply to remain equivocal and hold both sides."

sentences.zh: 時人由是號為“蘇模棱”。

translations.literal: People of the time therefore styled him "Su the Equivocator."
translations.idiomatic: From this people of the day nicknamed him "Su the Equivocator."

sentences.zh: 長安中，請還鄉改葬其父，優製令州縣供其葬事。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he requested leave to return home and rebury his father; an imperial edict of favor ordered the prefectures and counties to supply his funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he requested leave to return home and rebury his father; an edict of special favor ordered the prefectures and counties to supply his funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 味道因此侵毀鄉人墓田，役使過度，為憲司所劾，左授坊州刺史。

translations.literal: Weidao thereupon encroached on and destroyed the grave lands of his fellow townsmen and overworked the laborers; the censorate impeached him and he was demoted to prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao thereupon encroached on and destroyed his neighbors' grave lands and overworked the laborers; the censorate impeached him and he was demoted to prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed chief administrator of the metropolitan prefecture of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以親附張易之，昌宗貶授郿州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, for his close association with Zhang Yizhi and Changzong, he was demoted and sent out as prefect of Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong, for his close association with Zhang Yizhi and Changzong, he was demoted to prefect of Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄而復為益州大都督府長史，未行而卒，年五十八，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan prefecture, but died before taking up the post, at age fifty-eight; he was posthumously awarded the post of prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan prefecture, but died before taking up the post at the age of fifty-eight; he was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 味道與其弟太子洗馬味玄甚相友愛，味玄若請托不諧，輒麵加淩折，味道對之怡然，不以為忤，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: Weidao and his younger brother Weixuan, attendant of the crown prince's stables, were deeply fond of one another; whenever Weixuan's requests went unmet he would openly humiliate Weidao, who received this calmly and took no offense, for which commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao and his younger brother Weixuan, attendant of the crown prince's stables, were deeply devoted to each other. Whenever Weixuan's requests went unfulfilled he would openly humiliate his brother, yet Weidao received it calmly and took no offense, and commentators praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 有文集行於代。

translations.literal: A collected works circulated in the generation.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 李嶠

translations.literal: Li Jiao
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao

sentences.zh: 李嶠，趙州贊皇人，隋內史侍郎元操從曾孫也。

translations.literal: Li Jiao was a native of Zanhuang in Zhaozhou, a collateral great-great-grandson of Yuan Cao, interior secretary under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao came from Zanhuang in Zhaozhou and was a collateral great-great-grandson of Yuan Cao, interior secretary under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 代為著姓，父鎮惡，襄城令。

translations.literal: For generations they were a prominent clan; his father Zhen'e was magistrate of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been a prominent clan; his father Zhen'e was magistrate of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 嶠早孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jiao lost his father early and was famed for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was orphaned young and was famed for the filial devotion with which he served his mother.

sentences.zh: 為兒童時，夢有神人遺之雙筆，自是漸有學業。

translations.literal: As a child he dreamed that a divine being bestowed on him two writing brushes; from then on his scholarly attainment gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he dreamed that a divine being gave him two writing brushes, and from then on his scholarship gradually flourished.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，累轉監察御史。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and through successive appointments became investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive posts to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時嶺南邕、嚴二州首領反叛，發兵討擊，高宗令嶠往監軍事。

translations.literal: At that time the chieftains of Yong and Yan prefectures in Lingnan rebelled; troops were dispatched to suppress them, and Gaozong ordered Jiao to go oversee the military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chieftains of Yong and Yan prefectures in Lingnan rebelled; when troops were dispatched to suppress them, Gaozong ordered Jiao to go oversee the campaign.

sentences.zh: 嶠乃宣朝旨，特赦其罪，親入獠洞以招諭之。

translations.literal: Jiao thereupon announced the court's intent, specially pardoned their crimes, and entered the tribal stockades in person to summon and persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao thereupon proclaimed the court's intent, specially pardoned their crimes, and entered the tribal stockades in person to win them over.

sentences.zh: 叛者盡降，因罷兵而還，高宗甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The rebels all surrendered; he therefore disbanded the army and returned, and Gaozong greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all surrendered; he disbanded the army and returned, and Gaozong highly praised him.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to gentleman-attendant.

sentences.zh: 時酷吏來俊臣構陷狄仁傑、李嗣真、裴宣禮等三家，奏請誅之，則天使嶠與大理少卿張德裕、侍御史劉憲覆其獄。

translations.literal: At that time the cruel official Lai Junchen framed the three families of Di Renjie, Li Sizhen, and Pei Xuanli and memorialized requesting their execution; Empress Wu ordered Jiao, together with vice director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Deyu and attendant censor Liu Xian, to re-examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the cruel official Lai Junchen framed the families of Di Renjie, Li Sizhen, and Pei Xuanli and memorialized requesting their execution; Empress Wu ordered Jiao, together with vice director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Deyu and attendant censor Liu Xian, to re-examine the case.

sentences.zh: 德裕等雖知其枉，懼罪，並從俊臣所奏，嶠曰：“豈有知其枉濫而不為申明哉！

translations.literal: Deyu and the others, though knowing the injustice, feared punishment and all agreed with Junchen's memorial; Jiao said, "How can one know of wrongful persecution and not speak to clear it!
translations.idiomatic: Deyu and the others, though they knew the case was unjust, feared punishment and all sided with Junchen's memorial. Jiao said, "How can one know that injustice has been done and yet fail to speak in their defense!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：‘見義不為，無勇也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'To see what is righteous and not act is cowardice.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'To see what is righteous and not act is cowardice.'

sentences.zh: ’”乃與德裕等列其枉狀，由是忤旨，出為潤州司馬。

translations.literal: " He then joined Deyu and the others in setting forth the facts of the injustice; for this he went against the imperial will and was sent out as military aide of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He then joined Deyu and the others in setting forth the facts of the injustice; for this he ran afoul of the imperial will and was sent out as military aide of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔入，轉鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: By imperial summons he returned to court and was transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back to court, he was transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 則天深加接待，朝廷每有大手筆，皆特令嶠為之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu received him with deep favor; whenever the court needed a major composition, she always specially ordered Jiao to write it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu received him with marked favor, and whenever the court required a major composition she always specially charged Jiao with writing it.

sentences.zh: 時初置右御史台，巡按天下，嶠上疏陳其得失曰：陛下創置右台，分巡天下，察吏人善惡，觀風俗得失，斯政途之綱紀，禮法之準繩，無以加也。

translations.literal: At that time the Right Censorate had just been established to inspect throughout the realm; Jiao submitted a memorial stating its strengths and weaknesses, saying: "Your Majesty has newly established the Right Censorate, dispatching it to inspect throughout the realm, examining officials and people for good and evil, observing the gains and losses of local custom—this is the backbone of the path of governance and the measuring rod of ritual and law; nothing could surpass it."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Right Censorate had just been established to inspect the empire; Jiao submitted a memorial on its strengths and weaknesses, saying: "Your Majesty's new Right Censorate, sent out to inspect the realm, examine the conduct of officials and people, and observe local custom, is the backbone of governance and the standard of ritual and law, and nothing could improve upon it."

sentences.zh: 然猶有未折衷者，臣請試論之。

translations.literal: Yet there are still matters not yet reconciled; your servant requests permission to discuss them briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some points remain unsettled; I beg leave to discuss them briefly.

sentences.zh: 夫禁綱尚疏，法令宜簡，簡則法易行而不煩雜，疏則所羅廣而無苛碎。

translations.literal: As for prohibitions and regulatory nets, it is best they be loosely woven; laws and ordinances should be kept simple—simplicity makes the law easy to enforce without complexity, looseness makes what is covered broad without petty minutiae.
translations.idiomatic: Prohibitory regulations should be kept broad, and laws kept simple—simplicity makes enforcement easy and avoids needless complexity, while breadth of scope covers much without petty intrusion.

sentences.zh: 竊見垂拱二年諸道巡察使所奏科目，凡有四十四件，至於別準格敕令察訪者，又有三十餘條。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that in the second year of the Chuigong era the inspection categories reported by the inspection commissioners of the various circuits totaled forty-four items; as for separate items based on statutes, edicts, and orders for inspection, there were also more than thirty additional articles.
translations.idiomatic: I note that in the second year of the Chuigong era the inspection commissioners of the various circuits reported upon forty-four inspection categories, and that separate items drawn from statutes, edicts, and orders added more than thirty articles.

sentences.zh: 而巡察使率是三月已後出都，十一月終奏事，時限迫促，簿書填委，晝夜奔逐，以赴限期。

translations.literal: Yet inspection commissioners as a rule depart the capital after the third month and submit their reports by the end of the eleventh month—the time limit is pressing, documents pile up thick, they rush day and night to meet the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inspection commissioners typically leave the capital after the third month and must file their reports by the end of the eleventh month—a tight deadline that fills their desks with paperwork and keeps them racing day and night.

sentences.zh: 而每道所察文武官，多至二千餘人，少者一千已下，皆須品量才行，褒貶得失，欲令曲盡行能，則皆不暇。

translations.literal: In each circuit the civil and military officials inspected number as many as more than two thousand, or no fewer than below one thousand—all must be graded for talent and conduct, praised or blamed for gains and losses; if one wishes exhaustively to cover everyone's performance and capacity, there is no time for any of it.
translations.idiomatic: In each circuit they must inspect civil and military officials—often more than two thousand, never fewer than a thousand—all of whom must be graded for talent and conduct and commended or censured for their merits and faults; if they are to cover every officer's full record, they simply have no time.

sentences.zh: 此非敢墮於職而慢於官也，實才有限而力不及耳。

translations.literal: This is not because they dare fall short in duty and treat their office lightly; it is truly that talent is limited and strength does not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: This is not dereliction of duty or contempt for office—it is simply that their talent is limited and their strength falls short.

sentences.zh: 臣望量其功程，與其節製，使器周於用，力濟於時，然後進退可以責成，得失可以精覈矣。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes to measure the scope of their work and regulate their limits, so that capacity matches the task and strength meets the demands of the time—only then can promotion and dismissal be held accountable for results, and gains and losses be carefully verified.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that their workload be measured and bounded so that capacity matches the task and effort fits the time—only then can appointments and removals be held to account and outcomes judged with precision.

sentences.zh: 又曰：今之所察，但準漢之六條，推而廣之，則無不包矣。

translations.literal: He further said: What is inspected today need only follow the Six Articles of Han—extend and broaden them, and nothing would fall outside their scope.
translations.idiomatic: He further said: Today's inspections need only follow the Han Six Articles; extend them, and nothing would lie outside their scope.

sentences.zh: 無為多張科目，空費簿書。

translations.literal: There is no need to multiply inspection categories wastefully and empty effort into documents and registers.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to multiply inspection categories and waste effort on paperwork.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷萬機，非無事也，機事之動，恒在四方，是故冠蓋相望，郵驛繼踵。

translations.literal: Moreover the court has ten thousand affairs—it is not that there is nothing to do; when urgent matters arise, they are always in the four directions, which is why official carriages and canopies follow one after another and courier posts come in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The court's myriad affairs are never idle; when urgent business arises it is usually in the provinces, which is why official carriages follow one after another and courier traffic is unceasing.

sentences.zh: 今巡使既出，其他外州之事，悉當委之，則傳驛大減矣。

translations.literal: Now that inspection commissioners have already gone out, all other affairs of outer provinces should likewise be entrusted to them—then relay traffic would be greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: With inspection commissioners already in the field, other provincial affairs could all be entrusted to them as well, and courier traffic would drop sharply.

sentences.zh: 然則御史之職，故不可得閑，自非分州統理，無由濟其繁務。

translations.literal: Thus the duties of censor officials naturally cannot be idle; unless they are assigned to govern circuits in division, there is no way to manage the heavy workload.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial duties cannot be left idle; without assigning censors to govern grouped prefectures, there is no way to manage such overwhelming work.

sentences.zh: 請大小相兼，率十州置御史一人，以周年為限，使其親至屬縣，或入閭裏，督察奸訛，觀采風俗，然後可以求其實效，課其成功。

translations.literal: I ask that large and small [circuits] be combined, setting one censor for every ten prefectures on average, with a term of one full year, allowing them to reach subordinate counties in person or enter lanes and hamlets, investigate fraud and error, observe and gather local custom—only then can real results be sought and success assessed.
translations.idiomatic: I propose combining larger and smaller jurisdictions, assigning one censor for every ten prefectures on average for a one-year term, with time to reach subordinate counties in person or walk the lanes to investigate fraud and observe local custom—only then can real results be demanded and success measured.

sentences.zh: 若此法果行，必大裨政化。

translations.literal: If this method is truly carried out, it will greatly aid governance and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If this plan is adopted, it will greatly strengthen government.

sentences.zh: 且御史出持霜簡，入奏天闕，其於勵已自修，奉職存憲，比於他吏，可相百也。

translations.literal: Moreover censors going out hold the frost tablets; entering they report at the heavenly gate—in encouraging self-discipline and self-cultivation, in fulfilling office and preserving the statutes, compared with other officials they may be counted a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Censors go out bearing the frost tablets and return to report at the imperial gate; in self-discipline, faithful service, and upholding the law they exceed other officials a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 若其按劾奸邪，糾擿欺隱，比於他吏，可相十也。

translations.literal: If in investigating and impeaching the wicked and deceitful, exposing and plucking out concealment and fraud, compared with other officials they may be counted tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: In investigating wickedness and exposing fraud and concealment, they surpass other officials tenfold.

sentences.zh: 陛下試用臣言，妙擇賢能，委之心膂，假溫言以製之，陳賞罰以勸之，則莫不盡力而效死矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, if you trial my words, finely select the worthy and capable, entrust them as backbone, lend warm words to restrain them and set forth rewards and punishments to encourage them—then none will fail to exert their utmost strength and render service unto death.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty puts my proposal to the test, selects the best men, entrusts them as your inner counsellors, governs them with gracious words, and encourages them with rewards and punishments, none will fail to give their all—even unto death.

sentences.zh: 何政事之不理，何禁令之不行，何妖孽之敢興？

translations.literal: How could governance fail to be ordered? How could prohibitions fail to be enforced? How could evil omens dare to arise?
translations.idiomatic: What affair of state would go ungoverned? What prohibition would fail to be enforced? What evil omen would dare to arise?

sentences.zh: 則天善之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu approved of it.

sentences.zh: 乃下製分天下為二十道，簡擇堪為使者。

translations.literal: She issued an edict dividing the realm into twenty circuits and selecting men fit to serve as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: She issued an edict dividing the realm into twenty circuits and selecting men fit to serve as envoys.

sentences.zh: 會有沮議者，竟不行。

translations.literal: When opponents obstructed the plan, it was ultimately not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When opponents obstructed the plan, it was ultimately not carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋知天官侍郎事，遷麟台少監。

translations.literal: Soon he took charge of the vice ministry of the heaven office and was transferred to vice director of the Forest Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took charge of the vice ministry of the heaven office and was transferred to vice director of the Forest Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，與姚崇偕遷同鳳閣鸞台平章事，俄轉鸞台侍郎，依舊平章事，兼修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenli he was promoted together with Yao Chong to co-signatory of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace affairs; soon he was transferred to secretary of the Luan Terrace, continuing as co-signatory and also charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenli he was promoted together with Yao Chong to co-signatory of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace affairs; soon he was transferred to secretary of the Luan Terrace, continuing as co-signatory and also charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 久視元年，嶠舅天官侍郎張錫入知政事，嶠轉成均祭酒，罷知政事及修史，舅甥相繼在相位，時人榮之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiushi, Jiao's maternal uncle Zhang Xi, vice minister of the heaven office, entered the chief ministership; Jiao was transferred to libationer of the Directorate of Education and removed from the chief ministership and from compiling history. Uncle and nephew holding the chief ministership in succession was envied by people of the day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiushi Jiao's maternal uncle Zhang Xi, vice minister of the heaven office, entered the chief ministership; Jiao was transferred to libationer of the Directorate of Education and removed from the chief ministership and from compiling history. Uncle and nephew holding the chief ministership in succession was envied by people of the day.

sentences.zh: 嶠尋檢校文昌左丞、東都留守。

translations.literal: Jiao was soon made acting vice director of the Left Secretariat and guardian of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was soon made acting vice director of the Left Secretariat and guardian of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，嶠復以本官平章事，尋知納言事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an, Jiao again served as co-signatory in his former rank; soon he took charge of the chief secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chang'an Jiao again served as co-signatory in his former rank; soon he took charge of the chief secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷內史。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to interior secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to interior secretary.

sentences.zh: 嶠後固辭煩劇，復拜成均祭酒，平章事如故。

translations.literal: Jiao later firmly declined the burdensome duties and was again appointed libationer of the Directorate of Education, while continuing as co-signatory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao later firmly declined the burdensome duties and was again appointed libationer of the Directorate of Education, while continuing as co-signatory.

sentences.zh: 長安末，則天將建大像於白司馬阪，嶠上疏諫之，其略曰：“臣以法王慈敏，菩薩護持，唯擬饒益眾生，非要營修土木。

translations.literal: At the end of Chang'an, Empress Wu was about to erect a great image at White Horse Slope; Jiao submitted a remonstrance memorial, of which the gist was: "Your subject considers that the Dharma King is compassionate and wise and bodhisattvas protect and sustain us—the intent is only to enrich the lives of the masses, not to build in earth and wood.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chang'an era Empress Wu was about to erect a great image at White Horse Slope; Jiao submitted a remonstrance memorial, in which he said in summary: "Your subject considers that the Dharma King is compassionate and wise and that bodhisattvas protect and sustain us—the aim is only to enrich the lives of the people, not to raise structures of earth and timber.

sentences.zh: 伏聞適像，稅非戶口，錢出僧尼，不得州縣祗承，必是不能濟辦，終須科率，豈免勞擾！

translations.literal: I have heard that for this image the levy is not assessed on registered households and the money comes from monks and nuns; if the prefectures and counties cannot supply it, it surely cannot be fully raised and will ultimately require compulsory exactions—how can labor and distress be avoided!
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that for this image the levy is not assessed on registered households and the funds come from monks and nuns; if the prefectures and counties cannot meet the demand, the project surely cannot be fully financed and compulsory exactions will ultimately be required—how can the people escape hardship and distress!

sentences.zh: 天下編戶，貧弱者眾，亦有傭力客作以濟餱糧，亦有賣舍貼田以供王役。

translations.literal: Among registered households across the realm the poor and weak are many; some hire themselves out as laborers to earn their food, and some sell their houses or mortgage their fields to meet corvée duties.
translations.idiomatic: Among registered households across the realm the poor and weak are many; some hire themselves out as laborers to earn their food, and some sell their houses or mortgage their fields to meet corvée duties.

sentences.zh: 造像錢見有一十七萬餘貫，若將散施，廣濟貧窮，人與一千，濟得一十七萬餘戶。

translations.literal: The funds for the image currently amount to more than one hundred seventy thousand strings of cash; if dispersed in charity to relieve the poor widely, giving one thousand per person would succor more than one hundred seventy thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The funds for the image currently amount to more than one hundred seventy thousand strings of cash; if dispersed in charity to relieve the poor widely, giving one thousand per person would succor more than one hundred seventy thousand households.

sentences.zh: 拯饑寒之弊，省勞役之勤，順諸佛慈悲之心，沾聖君亭育之意，人神胥悅，功德無窮。”

translations.literal: Saving them from hunger and cold, sparing them the toil of corvée, conforming to the compassionate heart of all buddhas, and partaking of the nurturing intent of the sage ruler—humans and spirits alike would rejoice and the merit would be boundless."
translations.idiomatic: Saving them from hunger and cold, sparing them the toil of corvée, conforming to the compassionate heart of all buddhas, and partaking of the nurturing intent of the sage ruler—humans and spirits alike would rejoice and the merit would be boundless."

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，嶠以附會張易之兄弟，出為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong acceded, Jiao was sent out as prefect of Yu Prefecture for currying favor with Zhang Yizhi and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong acceded, Jiao was sent out as prefect of Yu Prefecture for currying favor with Zhang Yizhi and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 未行，又貶為通州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post he was further demoted to prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was further demoted to prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數月，徵拜吏部侍郎，封讚皇縣男。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, enfeoffed as baron of Zanhuang County.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, enfeoffed as baron of Zanhuang County.

sentences.zh: 無幾，遷吏部尚書，進封縣公。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to minister of personnel and promoted to county marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to minister of personnel and promoted to county marquis.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，代韋安石為中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong he replaced Wei Anshi as director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenlong he replaced Wei Anshi as director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，嶠在吏部時，誌欲曲行私惠。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Jiao was at the Ministry of Personnel, he had intended to distribute private favors broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Jiao was at the Ministry of Personnel, he had intended to distribute private favors broadly.

sentences.zh: 冀得復居相位奏置員外官數千人。

translations.literal: Hoping to regain the chief ministership, he memorialized to establish several thousand supernumerary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Hoping to regain the chief ministership, he memorialized to establish several thousand supernumerary officials.

sentences.zh: 至是官僚倍多，府庫減耗，乃抗表引咎辭職，並陳利害十餘事。

translations.literal: By then the bureaucracy had more than doubled and the treasury was depleted; he therefore submitted a forthright memorial accepting blame and resigning, setting forth more than ten points of benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: By then the bureaucracy had more than doubled and the treasury was depleted; he therefore submitted a forthright memorial accepting blame and resigning, setting forth more than ten points of benefit and harm.

sentences.zh: 中宗以嶠昌言時政之失，輒請罷免，手製慰諭而不允，尋令復居舊職。

translations.literal: Zhongzong, because Jiao plainly spoke of flaws in current policy and immediately requested dismissal, wrote in his own hand to comfort and reassure him and did not accept; soon he was ordered to resume his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiao plainly spoke of flaws in current policy and immediately requested dismissal, Zhongzong wrote in his own hand to comfort and reassure him and did not accept; soon Jiao was ordered to resume his former post.

sentences.zh: 三年，又加修文館大學士，監修國史，封趙國公。

translations.literal: In the third year he was further made grand academician of the Xiuwen Hall and supervisor of compiling the national history, enfeoffed as duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was further made grand academician of the Xiuwen Hall and supervisor of compiling the national history, enfeoffed as duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，罷中書令，以特進守兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong he was removed as director of the secretariat and made specially advanced, retaining the post of minister of war and made associate of the secretariat and chancellery of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jinglong he was removed as director of the secretariat and made specially advanced, retaining the post of minister of war and made associate of the secretariat and chancellery of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，出為懷州刺史，尋以年老致仕。

translations.literal: When Ruizong acceded he was sent out as prefect of Huai Prefecture, and soon retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong acceded he was sent out as prefect of Huai Prefecture, and soon retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗崩，嶠密表請處置相王諸子，勿令在京。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongzong died, Jiao had secretly memorialized requesting that the Prince of Xiang's sons be dealt with and not kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhongzong died, Jiao had secretly memorialized requesting that the Prince of Xiang's sons be dealt with and not kept in the capital.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗踐祚，宮內獲其表，以示侍臣。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, the palace obtained this memorial and showed it to the attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, the palace obtained this memorial and showed it to the attending ministers.

sentences.zh: 或請誅之，中書令張說曰：“嶠雖不辯逆順，然亦為當時之謀，吠非其主，不可追討其罪。”

translations.literal: Some requested his execution; director of the secretariat Zhang Shuo said, "Although Jiao did not distinguish loyalty from rebellion, he was also scheming for his own day—a dog barks at one who is not its master; his crime should not be pursued retroactively."
translations.idiomatic: Some requested his execution; director of the secretariat Zhang Shuo said, "Although Jiao did not distinguish loyalty from rebellion, he was also scheming for his own day—a dog barks at one who is not its master; his crime should not be pursued retroactively."

sentences.zh: 上從其言，乃下製曰：“事君之節，危而不變，為臣則忠，貳乃無赦。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his counsel and issued an edict saying: "The integrity of serving one's ruler is not to change in peril; for a minister loyalty is the law, and duplicity admits no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his counsel and issued an edict saying: "The integrity of serving one's ruler is not to change in peril; for a minister loyalty is the law, and duplicity admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: 特進、趙國公李嶠，往緣宗、韋弑逆，朕恭行戡定，揖讓之際，天命有歸，嶠有窺覦，不知逆順，狀陳詭計，朕親覽焉。

translations.literal: Specially advanced Duke of Zhao Li Jiao: formerly, when the Zong and Wei factions committed regicide, I respectfully restored order; at the moment of yielding and succession the mandate of Heaven had its rightful place, yet Jiao looked on with covetous eyes, not knowing loyalty from rebellion, and in his memorial set forth treacherous designs, which I have read with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Specially advanced Duke of Zhao Li Jiao: formerly, when the Zong and Wei factions committed regicide, I respectfully restored order; at the moment of yielding and succession the mandate of Heaven had its rightful place, yet Jiao looked on with covetous eyes, not knowing loyalty from rebellion, and in his memorial set forth treacherous designs, which I have read with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 以其早負辭學，累居台輔，忍而莫言，特掩其惡。

translations.literal: Because he long possessed literary learning and had repeatedly held chief ministerial posts, I have borne with him in silence and specially concealed his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Because he long possessed literary learning and had repeatedly held chief ministerial posts, I have borne with him in silence and specially concealed his wickedness.

sentences.zh: 今忠邪既辨，具物惟新，賞罰倘乖，下人安勸？

translations.literal: Now that loyalty and treachery have been distinguished and all things are renewed, if reward and punishment should be errant, how will those below be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Now that loyalty and treachery have been distinguished and all things are renewed, if reward and punishment should be errant, how will those below be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 雖經赦令，猶宜放斥，矜其老疾，俾遂餘生，宜聽隨子虔州刺史暢赴任。”

translations.literal: Although he has been covered by amnesty, he should still be dismissed; considering his age and illness, let him live out his remaining years—he should be permitted to follow his son Chang, prefect of Qian Prefecture, to his post."
translations.idiomatic: Although he has been covered by amnesty, he should still be dismissed; considering his age and illness, let him live out his remaining years—he should be permitted to follow his son Chang, prefect of Qian Prefecture, to his post."

sentences.zh: 尋起為盧州別駕而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as vice-prefect of Lu Prefecture but died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice-prefect of Lu Prefecture but died.

sentences.zh: 有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 崔融

translations.literal: Cui Rong
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong

sentences.zh: 崔融，齊州全節人。

translations.literal: Cui Rong was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong came from Quanjie in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，應八科舉擢第。

translations.literal: At first he passed the eight-field examination and was selected.
translations.idiomatic: At first he passed the eight-field examination and was selected.

sentences.zh: 累補宮門丞，兼直崇文館學士。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he became gate commissioner and concurrently a resident scholar of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive appointments he became gate commissioner and concurrently a resident scholar of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗在春宮，製融為侍讀，兼侍屬文，東朝表疏，多成其手。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince he appointed Rong reader-in-attendance and also charged him with composing documents; most of the eastern palace memorials and reports were written by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was crown prince he appointed Rong reader-in-attendance and also charged him with composing documents; most of the eastern palace memorials and reports were written by his hand.

sentences.zh: 聖曆中，則天幸嵩嶽，見融所撰《啟母廟碑》，深加歎美，及封禪畢，乃命融撰朝觀碑文。

translations.literal: During Shenli Empress Wu visited Mount Song, saw the Stele of the Qimu Temple Rong had composed, and greatly admired it; after the Feng and Shan rites were completed she ordered Rong to compose the court audience stele text.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenli Empress Wu visited Mount Song, saw the Stele of the Qimu Temple that Rong had composed, and greatly admired it; after the Feng and Shan rites were completed she ordered Rong to compose the court audience stele text.

sentences.zh: 自魏州司功參軍擢授著作佐郎，尋轉右史。

translations.literal: From recorder of Wei Prefecture he was elevated to assistant director of the Office for Writing the History, and soon transferred to right historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: From recorder of Wei Prefecture he was elevated to assistant director of the Office for Writing the History, and soon transferred to right historiographer.

sentences.zh: 聖曆二年，除著作郎，仍兼右史內供奉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenli he was appointed director of the Office for Writing the History, still concurrently serving as right historiographer within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenli he was appointed director of the Office for Writing the History, still concurrently serving as right historiographer within the palace.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 久視元年，坐忤張昌宗意，左授婺州長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiushi, for offending Zhang Changzong, he was demoted to chief administrator of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiushi, for offending Zhang Changzong, he was demoted to chief administrator of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頃之，昌宗怒解，又請召為春官郎中，知制誥事。

translations.literal: Before long Changzong's anger subsided; Rong also requested recall and was appointed director of the spring office and charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Changzong's anger subsided; Rong also requested recall and was appointed director of the spring office and charged with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，再遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an he was again transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chang'an he was again transferred to secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三年，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was additionally charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was additionally charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 時有司表稅關市，融深以為不可，上疏諫曰：伏見有司稅關市事條，不限工商，但是行人盡稅者，臣謹按《周禮》九賦，其七日“關市之賦”。

translations.literal: At that time the relevant offices memorialized to tax market passes, and Cui Rong deeply considered this inadvisable; he submitted a remonstrance, saying: I humbly see the regulations of the relevant offices on taxing market passes—they do not restrict [the tax] to artisans and merchants, but tax all who pass through; I respectfully note that among the Nine Levies in the Rites of Zhou, the seventh is "the levy on markets and passes."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the relevant offices memorialized to levy taxes on market passes. Cui Rong strongly opposed this and submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: I humbly observe that under the regulations proposed by the relevant offices for taxing market passes, there is no restriction to artisans and merchants—all travelers would be taxed. I respectfully note that among the Nine Levies in the Rites of Zhou, the seventh is "the levy on markets and passes."

sentences.zh: 竊惟市縱繁巧，關通末遊，欲令此徒止抑，所以鹹增賦稅。

translations.literal: I secretly consider that markets abound with cunning crafts and passes connect secondary pursuits—wishing to make these people cease and be restrained, therefore broadly increase levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: I gather the intent is that markets teem with cunning crafts and passes channel secondary pursuits—the hope is to restrain such people, and therefore levies are to be increased broadly.

sentences.zh: 臣謹商度今古，料量家國，竊將為不可稅。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully weighs past and present, estimates state and household, and privately considers [this] cannot be taxed.
translations.idiomatic: I have carefully weighed past and present and reckoned the interests of state and household, and I believe it cannot be taxed.

sentences.zh: 謹件事跡如左，伏惟聖旨擇焉。

translations.literal: I respectfully set forth the facts as follows; I humbly hope Your Sagely Intent will choose among them.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set forth the facts below and humbly ask that Your Majesty's judgment decide among them.

sentences.zh: 往古之時，淳樸未散，公田籍而不稅，關防譏而不征。

translations.literal: In ancient times, simplicity and purity had not yet dispersed—public fields were registered but not taxed; passes and barriers checked but did not levy.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when society was still unsophisticated, public fields were registered but not taxed, and passes and barriers inspected travelers but imposed no levies.

sentences.zh: 中代已來，澆風驟進，桑麻疲弊，稼穡辛勤，於是各徇通財，爭趨作巧，求徑捷之欲速，忘歲計之無餘。

translations.literal: From the middle ages onward, dissolute customs advanced swiftly; mulberry and hemp wore out, fieldwork grew laborious—thereupon each pursued circulating wealth, vied to pursue craftsmanship, seeking short cuts for speed, forgetting yearly reckoning left no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: From the middle ages onward, decadent customs spread rapidly. Mulberry and hemp production declined, farming grew ever more arduous, and people pursued circulating wealth, competed in craftsmanship, chased quick gains by shortcuts, and forgot that annual reckoning left nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 遂使田萊日荒，倉廩不積，蠶織休廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon fields daily grew waste, granaries did not accumulate, sericulture and weaving ceased and were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The result was that fields fell daily into neglect, granaries went unfilled, and sericulture and weaving were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 弊縕闕如，饑寒猥臻，亂離斯起。

translations.literal: Worn-out cotton garments were wanting; hunger and cold together arrived; disorder and dispersion arose thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Clothing fell into shortage, hunger and cold came in their wake, and disorder and upheaval arose.

sentences.zh: 先王懲其若此，所以變古隨時，依本者恒科，占末者增稅。

translations.literal: Former kings took warning from this—that is why they changed ancient ways according to the times: those based on fundamentals received fixed dues; those occupying secondary pursuits received increased taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings took warning from this, which is why they adapted ancient ways to changing times: those engaged in basic occupations paid regular dues, while those in secondary pursuits faced added taxes.

sentences.zh: 夫關市之稅者，謂市及國門，關門者也，唯斂出入之商賈，不稅來往之行人。

translations.literal: As for the tax on passes and markets, it refers to markets and the national gate—the gate of the pass—[it] only collects from merchants entering and leaving, not taxing travelers coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: The tax on passes and markets applied to markets and to the national gate—the gate of a pass—and only collected from merchants entering and leaving, not from ordinary travelers passing through.

sentences.zh: 今若不論商人，通取諸色，事不師古，法乃任情。

translations.literal: Now if merchants are not distinguished and all categories are universally taken, the matter does not take antiquity as teacher; the law is merely arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: If today merchants are not distinguished and every category is taxed alike, the policy does not follow the ancients and the law becomes arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 悠悠末代，於何瞻仰；

translations.literal: In this far-off degenerate age, toward what shall one look up?
translations.idiomatic: In this distant degenerate age, to what can one look for guidance?

sentences.zh: 濟濟盛朝，自取嗤笑。

translations.literal: In this flourishing court, full and splendid, [we] bring ridicule upon ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: In this flourishing court, we invite ridicule upon ourselves.

sentences.zh: 雖欲憲章姬典，乃是違背《周官》。

translations.literal: Although one wishes to take as model the Ji [Zhou] canon, this is in fact to violate the Rites of Zhou officials.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one wishes to take the Zhou canon as model, this in fact violates the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 臣知其不可者一也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows one reason why it is inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I know one reason why this will not work.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案《易》《係辭》稱：“庖羲氏沒，神農氏作，日中為市，致天下之人，聚天下之貨，交易而退，各得其所。”

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes that the "Attached Words" of the Changes states: "When Fuxi passed away, Shennong arose; he made markets at midday, bringing together the people under Heaven, gathering the goods under Heaven; they traded and departed, each obtaining what suited him."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that the Attached Words of the Book of Changes states: "When Fuxi passed away, Shennong arose. He established markets at midday, gathering people from across the realm and assembling goods from across the realm. They traded and withdrew, each obtaining what he needed."

sentences.zh: 《班志》亦云：“財者，帝王聚人守位，養成群生，奉順天德，理國安人之本也。

translations.literal: Ban's Treatise also says: "Wealth is the foundation by which emperors and kings gather people, secure their positions, nourish the multitudes, accord with Heaven's virtue, and order the state and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Treatise also says: "Wealth is the foundation by which emperors and kings gather people, secure their positions, nourish the multitudes, accord with Heaven's virtue, and govern the realm and settle the people.

sentences.zh: 仕農工商，四人有業。

translations.literal: Officials, farmers, artisans, and merchants—the four kinds of people each have their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, farmers, artisans, and merchants—the four classes each have their calling.

sentences.zh: 學以居位曰仕，辟士殖穀曰農，作巧成器曰工，通財鬻貨曰商。

translations.literal: Learning in order to hold office is called "officialdom"; opening soil and planting grain is called "agriculture"; making cunning and completing vessels is called "craftsmanship"; circulating wealth and selling goods is called "commerce."
translations.idiomatic: Learning in order to hold office is called "officialdom"; opening land and growing grain is "agriculture"; applying skill to fashion tools is "craftsmanship"; circulating wealth and selling goods is "commerce."

sentences.zh: 聖王量能授事，四人陳力受職。”

translations.literal: Sagely kings measured ability and assigned tasks; the four kinds of people displayed their strength and received office."
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings assigned duties according to capacity, and the four classes each applied their strength and received their roles."

sentences.zh: 然則四人各業久矣。

translations.literal: Thus the four kinds of people have each had their occupations for long.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the four classes have long had their distinct occupations.

sentences.zh: 今復安得動而搖之！

translations.literal: How can one now again move and shake them!
translations.idiomatic: How can we now move to shake them up!

sentences.zh: 蕭何云：“人情一定，不可復動。”

translations.literal: Xiao He said: "Once human sentiment is settled, it cannot be moved again."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He said: "Once custom is settled, it must not be disturbed again."

sentences.zh: 班固又云：曹參相齊，齊國安集，大稱賢相。

translations.literal: Ban Gu also said: Cao Can served as chancellor of Qi; Qi was settled and tranquil, and he was greatly praised as a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu also wrote: When Cao Can served as chancellor of Qi, Qi was settled and tranquil, and he was widely praised as a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 參去，屬其後相曰：“以齊獄市為寄，慎勿擾也。”

translations.literal: When Can departed, he entrusted to his successor, saying: "Take the prisons and markets of Qi as your charge—be careful not to disturb them."
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Can left office, he told his successor: "Regard the prisons and markets of Qi as your trust—be careful not to disturb them."

sentences.zh: 後相曰：“理無大於此者乎？”

translations.literal: The successor said, "Is there no principle greater than this?"
translations.idiomatic: The successor asked, "Is there any principle more important than this?"

sentences.zh: 參曰：“不然。

translations.literal: Can said, "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Can replied, "Not at all.

sentences.zh: 夫獄市者，所以並容也，今若擾之，奸人安所容乎？

translations.literal: As for prisons and markets, they serve to accommodate all alike; if one now disturbs them, where will wicked men find accommodation?
translations.idiomatic: Prisons and markets serve to accommodate all alike; if you disturb them, where will wrongdoers find refuge?

sentences.zh: 吾是以先之。”

translations.literal: I therefore placed priority on this."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I prioritized this."

sentences.zh: 夫獄市，兼受善惡。

translations.literal: As for prisons and markets, they jointly receive good and evil alike.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons and markets accommodate both the good and the wicked.

sentences.zh: 若窮極，奸人無所容竄；

translations.literal: If driven to extremity, wicked men have nowhere to hide and flee;
translations.idiomatic: If driven to extremity, the wicked have nowhere to hide;

sentences.zh: 奸人無所容竄，久且為亂。

translations.literal: when wicked men have nowhere to hide and flee, before long there will be disorder.
translations.idiomatic: when the wicked have nowhere to hide, disorder is not long in coming.

sentences.zh: 秦人極刑而天下叛，孝武峻法而刑獄繁，此其效也。

translations.literal: The Qin people used extreme punishments and the realm rebelled; Emperor Wu of Han used severe laws and prisons multiplied—such was their effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin used extreme punishments and the realm rebelled; Emperor Wu of Han used severe laws and prisons multiplied—such were the results.

sentences.zh: 老子曰：“我無為而人自化，我好靜而人自正。”

translations.literal: Laozi said: "If I do nothing, people transform themselves; if I love stillness, people right themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said: "When I do nothing, people transform themselves of their own accord; when I cherish stillness, people right themselves of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 參欲以道化其本，不欲擾其末。

translations.literal: Can wished to transform the root by the Way, not to disturb the branch-tips.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Can wished to transform the root through the Way, not to disturb the branches.

sentences.zh: 臣知其不可者二也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows the second reason why it is inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I know a second reason why this will not work.

sentences.zh: 四海之廣，九州之雜。

translations.literal: The Four Seas are vast; the Nine Provinces are diverse.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast and the provinces many and diverse.

sentences.zh: 關必據險路，市必憑要津。

translations.literal: Passes necessarily occupy perilous routes; markets necessarily rely on strategic fords.
translations.idiomatic: Passes necessarily stand on perilous routes; markets necessarily cluster at strategic crossings.

sentences.zh: 若乃富商大賈，豪宗惡少，輕死重義，結黨連群，喑鳴則彎弓，睚眥則挺劍。

translations.literal: Such being the case, great merchants and wealthy traders, powerful clans and wicked youths, who lightly esteem death and heavily esteem righteousness, form factions and join groups—at a low cry they bend the bow, at the least grievance they draw the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the great merchants and wealthy traders, powerful clans and reckless youths, who hold loyalty dearer than life, form factions and bands, bend their bows at the slightest signal, and draw their swords at the slightest offense.

sentences.zh: 小有失意，且猶如此，一旦變法，定是相驚。

translations.literal: Slightly displeased, they are already like this; once the law is changed, they are bound to alarm one another.
translations.idiomatic: Even when only slightly wronged they behave this way; once the law is changed, alarm is certain.

sentences.zh: 乘茲困窮，或致騷動，便恐南走越，北走胡，非唯流逆齊人，亦自攪亂殊俗。

translations.literal: Seizing this moment of hardship, they may give rise to unrest—for fear that some flee south to Yue, north to the Hu; not only would the people of Qi become rebellious refugees, they would also themselves stir up alien customs.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the opportunity of their hardship, unrest may erupt. People may flee south to Yue or north to the northern tribes—not only would common folk turn rebellious, but alien border peoples would also be thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 又如邊徼之地，寇賊為鄰，興胡之旅，歲月相繼，倘同科賦，致有猜疑，一從散亡，何以製禁？

translations.literal: Again, on the border marches, bandits and foes are neighbors; travelers raising the Hu come year after year in succession—if subject to the same categories of levies, suspicion will arise; once they scatter and flee, how can one restrain and forbid?
translations.idiomatic: And on the frontier marches, where bandits are neighbors and Hu travelers pass year after year, if they face the same taxes, suspicion will arise; once they scatter, how can they be controlled?

sentences.zh: 求利雖切，為害方深。

translations.literal: Though the quest for profit is keen, the harm is just then deep.
translations.idiomatic: Though the pursuit of profit is urgent, the harm will be far deeper.

sentences.zh: 而有司上言，不識大體，徒欲益帑藏，助軍國，殊不知軍國益擾，帑藏逾空。

translations.literal: Yet the relevant offices submit their words, not recognizing the larger pattern—merely wishing to enrich the vaults and support army and state, yet not knowing that army and state will grow ever more troubled and the vaults ever emptier.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the relevant offices submit this proposal without grasping the larger picture. They merely wish to fill the treasury and support the army and state, not realizing that the army and state will grow more troubled and the treasury ever emptier.

sentences.zh: 臣知其不可者三也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows the third reason why it is inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I know a third reason why this will not work.

sentences.zh: 孟軻又云：“古之為關也，將以禦暴；

translations.literal: Mencius also said: "In antiquity, passes were made to ward off violence;
translations.idiomatic: Mencius also said: "In antiquity, passes were established to keep out violence;

sentences.zh: 今之為關也，將以為暴。”

translations.literal: today passes are made to become violence."
translations.idiomatic: today passes are used to commit violence."

sentences.zh: 今行者皆稅，本末同流。

translations.literal: Now all travelers are taxed—the root and branch flow in one stream.
translations.idiomatic: Now all travelers are taxed, so fundamental and secondary pursuits are treated alike.

sentences.zh: 且如天下諸津，舟航所聚，旁通巴、漢，前指閩、越，七澤十藪，三江五湖，控引河洛，兼包淮海。

translations.literal: Moreover, like all the fords under Heaven where boats gather—connecting sideways with Ba and Han, pointing forward to Min and Yue, the seven marshes and ten marshlands, the Three Rivers and Five Lakes, drawing in the Yellow River and Luo, encompassing both Huai and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Consider all the river crossings under Heaven where boats congregate: they connect to Ba and Han in the west and reach Min and Yue in the southeast, threading through the seven marshes and ten marshlands, the Three Rivers and Five Lakes, drawing on the Yellow River and Luo, and spanning the Huai and Hai regions.

sentences.zh: 弘舸巨艦，千軸萬艘，交貿往還，昧旦永日。

translations.literal: Great vessels and huge ships, thousands of axles and tens of thousands of craft, commerce going and coming—from daybreak until day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Great vessels and huge ships—thousands upon tens of thousands of craft—trade back and forth from dawn until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 今若江津河口，置鋪納稅，納稅則檢覆，檢覆則遲留。

translations.literal: If now at river crossings and estuaries tax stations are set up to collect taxes, collecting taxes then requires inspection and verification, and inspection and verification then causes delay and detention.
translations.idiomatic: If tax stations are placed at river crossings and estuaries, collecting taxes requires inspection, and inspection causes delay.

sentences.zh: 此津才過，彼鋪復止，非唯國家稅錢，更遭主司僦賂。

translations.literal: Having just passed this ford, one is stopped again at that station—not only does the state take tax money; one further suffers extortion and bribes from the officials in charge.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner has a vessel cleared one crossing than it is halted at the next station. Merchants pay not only state taxes but also bribes extorted by officials.

sentences.zh: 船有大小，載有少多，量物而稅，觸途淹久。

translations.literal: Boats have large and small; loads have more and less; measuring goods to tax them—everywhere one touches the road, delays are long.
translations.idiomatic: Boats vary in size and cargoes in quantity; taxing goods by measurement means delays at every stop.

sentences.zh: 統論一日之中，未過十分之一，因此壅滯，必致籲嗟。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, in the course of a day not even one-tenth is passed; because of this obstruction and stagnation, sighs and complaints must result.
translations.idiomatic: On average, in a full day a vessel may not cover even one-tenth of its route. Such congestion inevitably provokes widespread complaint.

sentences.zh: 一朝失利，則萬商廢業，萬商廢業，則人不聊生。

translations.literal: Once in the morning profit is lost, then ten thousand merchants abandon their occupations; ten thousand merchants abandon their occupations, then people cannot preserve their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Once profits are lost, myriad merchants abandon their trades—and when myriad merchants abandon their trades, people cannot make a living.

sentences.zh: 其間或有輕訬任俠之徒，斬龍刺蛟之黨，鄱陽暴謔之客，富平悍壯之夫，居則藏鏹，出便竦劍。

translations.literal: Among them there may be lightly scornful, chivalrous gallants, dragon-slaying and flood-dragon stabbing partisans, Poyang's brutal revelers, Fuping's fierce stalwarts—at home they hoard money; abroad they brandish swords.
translations.idiomatic: Among them are reckless gallants and swashbucklers, dragon-slaying adventurers, brawlers from Poyang, fierce men from Fuping—who hoard silver at home and draw swords abroad.

sentences.zh: 加之以重稅，因之以威脅，一旦獸窮則搏，鳥窮則攫，執事者復何以安之哉？

translations.literal: Add to them heavy taxes, follow with intimidation—once beasts are cornered they strike, birds cornered they seize; how again can those in charge find peace?
translations.idiomatic: Add heavy taxes and follow with intimidation, and when beasts are cornered they fight and birds cornered they strike. How, then, can officials retain their peace?

sentences.zh: 臣知其不可者四也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows the fourth reason why it is inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I know a fourth reason why this will not work.

sentences.zh: 五帝之初，不可詳已；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Five Emperors, it cannot be examined in detail;
translations.idiomatic: The beginnings of the Five Emperors cannot be examined in detail;

sentences.zh: 三王之後，厥有著雲；

translations.literal: after the Three Kings, there are clear records;
translations.idiomatic: after the Three Sage Kings, clear records exist;

sentences.zh: 秦、漢相承，典章大備至如關市之稅，史籍有文。

translations.literal: Qin and Han succeeded each other; canons and regulations were greatly complete—as for the tax on passes and markets, the historical records contain entries.
translations.idiomatic: Through Qin and Han succession, institutions were fully established, and records of the tax on passes and markets exist in the historical texts.

sentences.zh: 秦政以雄圖武力，舍之而不用也；

translations.literal: Qin rule, with heroic designs and martial force, set it aside and did not use it;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin, with his grand ambitions and military power, set it aside and did not employ it;

sentences.zh: 漢武以霸略英才，去之而勿取也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, with hegemonic strategy and outstanding talent, removed it and did not take it up.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han, with his hegemonic strategy and outstanding talent, abolished it and would not restore it.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 關為禦暴之所，市為聚人之地，稅市則人散，稅關則暴興，暴興則起異圖，人散則懷不軌。

translations.literal: Passes are places for warding off violence; markets are places for gathering people. Tax markets and people scatter; tax passes and violence arises—violence arises and alien designs are stirred; people scatter and they harbor rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Passes were meant to keep out violence; markets were meant to gather people. Tax markets and people disperse; tax passes and violence rises. When violence rises, rebellious designs emerge; when people disperse, subversive intent takes hold.

sentences.zh: 夫人心莫不背善而樂禍，易動而難安。

translations.literal: Now human hearts all turn away from good and delight in calamity—they are easy to move but hard to settle.
translations.idiomatic: Human hearts naturally turn from good and delight in calamity; they are easily stirred but hard to pacify.

sentences.zh: 一市不安，則天下之市心搖矣；

translations.literal: One market unsettled, then the hearts of markets under Heaven are shaken;
translations.idiomatic: If one market is unsettled, the confidence of markets throughout the realm is shaken;

sentences.zh: 一關不安，則天下之關心動矣。

translations.literal: one pass unsettled, then the hearts of passes under Heaven are moved.
translations.idiomatic: if one pass is unsettled, anxiety spreads through every pass in the realm.

sentences.zh: 況澆風久扇，變法為難，徒欲禁末流、規小利，豈知失玄默、亂大倫。

translations.literal: Moreover, dissolute customs have long been fanned; changing laws is difficult—merely wishing to restrain branch streams and scheme for small profit, how could one know one loses dark silence and disrupts the great order?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, decadent customs have long prevailed and changing laws is difficult. Merely seeking to restrain secondary pursuits for small gain, one fails to see that this forfeits tranquil governance and disrupts the fundamental order.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉眇小，齊、隋齷齪，亦所不行斯道者也。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin were petty and small; Qi and Sui were sordid and cramped—they too did not carry out this policy.
translations.idiomatic: Even the petty regimes of Wei and Jin and the sordid dynasties of Qi and Sui did not pursue this policy.

sentences.zh: 臣知其不可者五也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows the fifth reason why it is inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I know a fifth reason why this will not work.

sentences.zh: 今之所以稅關市者，何也？

translations.literal: Now why tax passes and markets?
translations.idiomatic: Why is it, then, that passes and markets are to be taxed?

sentences.zh: 豈不以國用不足，邊寇為虞，一行斯術，冀有殷贍然也！

translations.literal: Is it not because state expenses are insufficient and border foes are a worry—carry out this method once, hoping for abundance and sufficiency!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not because state revenues are insufficient and border enemies cause concern—a hope that by implementing this measure, funds might become ample!

sentences.zh: 微臣敢借前箸以籌之。

translations.literal: This lowly subject dares borrow the chopsticks before him to reckon it.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject ventures to use the chopsticks of past sages to calculate the matter.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下當聖期，禦玄籙，沉璧於洛，刻石於嵩，鑄寶鼎以窮奸，坐明堂而布政，神化廣洽，至德潛通。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty occupies the sage period, holds the dark talisman, sank the jade disc in the Luo, carved stone at Song, cast the precious cauldron to exhaust wickedness, sat in the Bright Hall to distribute government—the divine transformation broadly harmonizes, the utmost virtue secretly pervades.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty occupies a sage age, holds the mandate of Heaven, performed the rite of sinking the jade disc in the Luo River, carved stone at Mount Song, cast the precious cauldron to expose evil, and seated himself in the Bright Hall to govern. Divine influence spreads widely and supreme virtue pervades all.

sentences.zh: 東夷暫驚，應時平殄；

translations.literal: The eastern Yi were briefly alarmed and promptly extinguished according to the time;
translations.idiomatic: The eastern barbarians were briefly alarmed and promptly subdued;

sentences.zh: 南蠻才動，計日歸降。

translations.literal: the southern Man had barely stirred when within numbered days they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: the southern tribes had barely stirred before they submitted within days.

sentences.zh: 西域五十餘國，廣輸一萬餘里，城堡清夷，亭堠靜謐。

translations.literal: More than fifty states of the Western Regions, extending over ten thousand li in breadth—fortresses clear and pacified, beacon towers quiet and serene.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty states of the Western Regions stretch over ten thousand li, their fortresses tranquil and their beacon towers quiet.

sentences.zh: 比為患者，唯苦二蕃。

translations.literal: Those who have lately been troublesome are only the two frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The only recent sources of trouble are the two frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃請命，邊事不起，即目雖尚屯兵，久後疑成馳柝。

translations.literal: Now Tibet requests orders and border affairs do not arise; at present troops are still stationed, but in time I suspect even the alarm-clapper will cease.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tibet has submitted and border incidents have ceased. Troops are still stationed for now, but in time even the border alarm may fall silent.

sentences.zh: 獨有默啜，假息孤恩，惡貫禍盈，覆亡不暇。

translations.literal: Only Mochuo, borrowing a breath on isolated favor—his evil run through, calamities full—has no leisure before overthrow and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Only Mochuo, living on borrowed time through Your Majesty's grace, has evil fulfilled and calamity full—his overthrow cannot be long delayed.

sentences.zh: 征役日已省矣，繁費日已稀矣，然猶下明製，遵太樸，愛人力，惜人財，王侯舊封，妃主新禮，所有支料，咸令減削。

translations.literal: Conscript service daily grows reduced, heavy expenses daily grow scarce—yet still edicts of clear regulation are issued, the great simplicity is followed, human labor is loved, human wealth is cherished—the old enfeoffments of kings and marquises, the new gifts of princesses and consorts, all provisions and supplies are uniformly ordered reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Conscription is already reduced daily and heavy expenditures grow ever rarer. Yet Your Majesty still issues clear edicts, observes great simplicity, cherishes human labor and treasure, and has ordered reductions in the stipends of enfeoffed nobles and the gifts of princesses and consorts alike.

sentences.zh: 此陛下以躬率先，堯、舜之用心也。

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty taking the lead in person—the mind of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: This is Your Majesty leading by personal example—the very spirit of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 且關中、河北，水旱數年，諸處逃亡，今始安輯，倘加重稅，或慮相驚。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Guanzhong and Hebei, flood and drought for several years; fugitives in many places have only now been settled—if heavy taxes are added, one fears mutual alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Guanzhong and Hebei have suffered flood and drought for years. Fugitives in many regions have only now been pacified; imposing heavy taxes may provoke widespread alarm.

sentences.zh: 況承平歲積，薄賦日久，俗荷深恩，人知自樂。

translations.literal: Moreover, years of peace accumulate; light levies have been long; customs bear deep grace, people know self-contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, years of peace have accumulated and light taxation has long prevailed. The people have enjoyed deep grace and know contentment.

sentences.zh: 卒有變法，必多生怨，生怨則驚擾，驚擾則不安，中既不安，外何能禦？

translations.literal: Suddenly there is change of law, necessarily many grievances arise; grievances arise then alarm and disturbance; alarm and disturbance then unrest—when the interior is already unsettled, how can the exterior be defended?
translations.idiomatic: A sudden change of law will inevitably breed widespread resentment. Resentment breeds alarm, alarm breeds unrest—and when the interior is unsettled, how can the exterior be defended?

sentences.zh: 文王曰：“帝王富其人，霸王富其地，理國若不足，亂國若有餘。”

translations.literal: King Wen said: "Emperors and kings enrich their people; hegemons and lords enrich their lands. A well-ordered state seems insufficient; a disorderly state seems to have surplus."
translations.idiomatic: King Wen said: "Emperors and kings enrich their people; hegemons enrich their territory. A well-governed state seems to have too little; a chaotic state seems to have too much."

sentences.zh: 古人有言：“帝王藏於天下，諸侯藏於百姓，農夫藏於庾，商賈藏於篋。”

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "Emperors and kings store [wealth] in the realm under Heaven; feudal lords store it in the common people; farmers store it in granaries; merchants store it in chests."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Emperors store wealth throughout the realm; feudal lords store it among the people; farmers store it in granaries; merchants store it in coffers."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下詳之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty examine this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 必若師興有費，國儲多窘，即請倍算商客，加斂平人。

translations.literal: If it must be that armies are raised and there are expenses, and state stores are greatly straitened, then please double-assess merchant travelers and add levies on common people.
translations.idiomatic: If military campaigns require funds and state reserves are strained, then by all means double the assessments on merchants and add levies on common folk.

sentences.zh: 如此則國保富強，人免憂懼，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Thus then the state preserves strength and wealth, people are spared worry and fear—the realm under Heaven is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: That would preserve national wealth and strength, spare the people worry and fear, and bring great fortune to the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣知其不可者六也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows the sixth reason why it is inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: I know a sixth reason why this will not work.

sentences.zh: 陛下留神係表，屬想政源，冒茲炎熾，早朝晏坐。

translations.literal: Your Majesty keeps mind on the attached memorial, fixes thought on the source of governance, braves this blazing heat—early court, late sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attends closely to memorials, fixes thought on the source of governance, braves this scorching heat, and holds court early and works late.

sentences.zh: 一日二日，機務不遺，先天後天，虛心密應。

translations.literal: Day after day, urgent affairs are not omitted; before Heaven, after Heaven—empty of mind, secretly responsive.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day, no urgent business is neglected. With openness before Heaven and responsiveness after Heaven, You respond with careful attention.

sentences.zh: 時政得失，小子何知，率陳瞽辭，伏紙惶懼。

translations.literal: The gains and losses of present governance—what does this petty fellow know? I frankly present blind words, prostrate on paper in fear and trepidation.
translations.idiomatic: What does one such as I know of the merits and faults of present policy? I frankly offer these blind words and submit this memorial in fear and trepidation.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，則天納之，乃寢其事。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; Empress Wu accepted it, and then shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Wu accepted it and shelved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年，除司禮少卿，仍知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites, still charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites, still charged with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 時張易之兄弟頗招集文學之士，融與納言李嶠、鳳閣侍郎蘇味道、麟台少監王紹宗等俱以文才降節事之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi and his brothers gathered many literary men; Rong, together with chief secretariat Li Jiao, secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao, vice director of the Forest Pavilion Wang Shaozong, and others, all lowered themselves to serve them for their literary talents.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yizhi and his brothers gathered many literary men; Rong, together with chief secretariat Li Jiao, secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao, vice director of the Forest Pavilion Wang Shaozong, and others, all lowered themselves to serve them for their literary talents.

sentences.zh: 及易之伏誅，融左授袁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed Rong was demoted to prefect of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi was executed Rong was demoted to prefect of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜國子司業，兼修國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed vice director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned and appointed vice director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，以預修《則天實錄》成，封清河縣子，賜物五百段，璽書褒美。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong, for his participation in completing the Veritable Records of Wu Zetian, he was enfeoffed as viscount of Qinghe County, granted five hundred rolls of goods, and commended in an imperial letter with the seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenlong, for his participation in completing the Veritable Records of Wu Zetian, he was enfeoffed as viscount of Qinghe County, granted five hundred rolls of goods, and commended in an imperial letter with the seal.

sentences.zh: 融為文典麗，當時罕有其比，朝廷所須《洛出寶圖頌》、《則天哀冊文》及諸大手筆，並手敕付融。

translations.literal: Rong's prose was classical and elegant, rarely matched in his day; the court's required compositions—the "Ode on the Precious Diagram Emerging from the Luo," the Lament Text for Wu Zetian, and other major works—were all handed to Rong by personal imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's prose was classical and elegant, rarely matched in his day; the court's required compositions—the "Ode on the Precious Diagram Emerging from the Luo," the Lament Text for Wu Zetian, and other major works—were all handed to Rong by personal imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 撰哀冊文，用思精苦，遂發病卒，時年五十四。

translations.literal: Composing the lament text, he strained his mind with extreme effort and fell ill and died, at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: While composing the lament text he strained his mind with extreme effort, fell ill, and died at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 以侍讀之恩，追贈衛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: In gratitude for his service as reader-in-attendance he was posthumously made prefect of Weizhou and given the posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In gratitude for his service as reader-in-attendance he was posthumously made prefect of Weizhou and given the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 有集六十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 二子禹錫、翹，開元中，相次為中書舍人。

translations.literal: His two sons Yuxi and Qiao, during Kaiyuan, successively served as secretaries of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Yuxi and Qiao, during Kaiyuan, successively served as secretaries of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 盧藏用

translations.literal: Lu Zangyong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zangyong

sentences.zh: 盧藏用，字子潛，度支尚書承慶之侄孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Zangyong, courtesy name Ziqian, was a grandnephew of Chengqing, minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zangyong, courtesy name Ziqian, was a grandnephew of Chengqing, minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 父敬，有名於時，官至魏州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Jing was famed in his day and rose to military aide of Wei Prefecture.
