translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was famed in his day and rose to military aide of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 藏用少以辭學著稱。

translations.literal: Zangyong was famed from youth for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zangyong was famed for his literary learning.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士選，不調，乃著《芳草賦》以見意。

translations.literal: At first he passed the jinshi selection but received no appointment; he therefore composed the "Rhapsody on Fragrant Herbs" to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: At first he passed the jinshi selection but received no appointment; he therefore composed the "Rhapsody on Fragrant Herbs" to express his intent.

sentences.zh: 尋隱居終南山，學辟穀、練氣之術。

translations.literal: Soon he retired to Mount Zhongnan and studied the arts of grain abstinence and breath cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired to Mount Zhongnan and studied the arts of grain abstinence and breath cultivation.

sentences.zh: 長安中，征拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: During Chang'an he was summoned and appointed left remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he was summoned and appointed left remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 時則天將營興泰宮於萬安山，藏用上疏諫曰：臣愚雖不達時變，竊嚐讀書，見自古帝王之跡眾矣。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Wu was about to build Xingtai Palace at Mount Wan'an. Zangyong submitted a memorial to remonstrate, saying: "This subject is foolish and, though I do not comprehend the changes of the times, I have privately read books and seen that the traces of emperors and kings since antiquity are many."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Wu was planning to construct Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an. Zangyong submitted a memorial in protest, saying: "Though I am but a foolish subject who does not grasp the changing times, in my private reading I have encountered countless examples of emperors and kings of old."

sentences.zh: 臣聞土階三尺，茅茨不翦，采椽不斫者，唐堯之德也；

translations.literal: I have heard that earthen steps three feet high, thatched roofs left untrimmed, and unhewn rafters of plain wood—these were the virtue of Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that Tang Yao's virtue lay in earthen steps three feet high, unshorn thatch, and unadorned wooden rafters.

sentences.zh: 卑宮室，菲飲食，盡力於溝洫者，大禹之行也；

translations.literal: Humbling the palace chambers, making food and drink frugal, and exerting all strength on ditches and canals—this was the conduct of Yu the Great.
translations.idiomatic: Yu the Great's way was to keep his dwellings modest, his fare simple, and to devote all his strength to digging canals and irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 惜中人十家之產，而罷露台之製者，漢文之明也。

translations.literal: Cherishing the property of ten middling households and abolishing the terrace-pavilion project—this was the wisdom of Emperor Wen of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han showed his wisdom when he spared the wealth of ten ordinary households and canceled plans for a terrace pavilion.

sentences.zh: 並能垂名無窮，為帝皇之烈。

translations.literal: All alike were able to leave their names to endure without end, becoming exemplars among emperors and sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: All of them won lasting renown and stand as great models among emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 豈不以克念徇物，博施濟眾，以臻於仁恕哉！

translations.literal: Was it not because they restrained their thoughts and yielded to material things, broadly dispensing benefits to relieve the multitude, thereby attaining benevolence and forbearance!
translations.idiomatic: Surely this was because they mastered their desires, set aside personal indulgence, and broadly gave aid to the people until they reached true benevolence and forbearance!

sentences.zh: 今陛下崇台邃宇，離宮別館，亦已多矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's lofty terraces and deep halls, detached palaces and separate lodges, are already many.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already has no lack of lofty towers, deep halls, detached palaces, and separate lodges.

sentences.zh: 更窮人之力以事土木，臣恐議者以陛下為不憂人、務奉已也。

translations.literal: Further exhausting people's strength to serve earthworks and timber construction—I fear critics will regard Your Majesty as not caring for the people and devoted to serving yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you further drain the people's strength for construction, I fear observers will take Your Majesty to be indifferent to the people's welfare and intent only on gratifying yourself.

sentences.zh: 且頃歲已來，雖年穀頗登，而百姓未有儲蓄。

translations.literal: Moreover, in recent years, though the annual grain harvest has been fairly abundant, the common people still have no savings.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in recent years, though harvests have been fairly good, the common people still have nothing put by.

sentences.zh: 陛下西幸東巡，人未休息，土木之役，歲月不空。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's journeys west and tours east—the people have not yet rested, and labors of earth and wood leave no month empty.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's journeys west and tours east, the people have had no respite, and construction work has left scarcely a month free.

sentences.zh: 陛下不因此時施德布化，復廣造宮苑，臣恐人未易堪。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, instead of using this time to spread virtue and disseminate transforming influence, again broadly builds palaces and gardens—I fear the people will not easily bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of using this moment to spread virtue and benevolent rule, Your Majesty would again expand palaces and gardens on a grand scale—I fear the people will find it hard to endure.

sentences.zh: 今左右近臣，多以順意為忠；

translations.literal: Now the close attendants at Your Majesty's side mostly take complying with your wishes to be loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Today those nearest Your Majesty mostly treat agreement with your wishes as loyalty.

sentences.zh: 朝廷具僚，皆以犯忤為患。

translations.literal: All officials of the court alike regard giving offense and contradiction as a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the court all treat speaking against Your Majesty as something to be dreaded.

sentences.zh: 至今陛下不知百姓失業，亦不知左右傷陛下之仁也。

translations.literal: To this day Your Majesty does not know the people's loss of livelihood, nor does Your Majesty know that those around you are harming Your Majesty's benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Even now Your Majesty remains unaware that the people have lost their livelihoods, and unaware that those around you are damaging Your Majesty's reputation for benevolence.

sentences.zh: 臣聞忠臣不避死亡之患，以納君於仁；

translations.literal: I have heard that loyal ministers do not avoid the peril of death, in order to lead the ruler into benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that loyal ministers do not shrink from the risk of death if by doing so they can guide their ruler toward benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 明主不惡切直之言，以垂名千載。

translations.literal: A wise ruler does not detest blunt and straight speech, in order to leave his name for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler does not resent frank and forthright counsel, for by accepting it he wins a name that endures for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能發明恕之製，以勞人為辭，則天下必以陛下為惜人力而苦己也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly enact measures of enlightened forbearance, taking the burden on the people as your reason, then all under Heaven will surely regard Your Majesty as cherishing human labor and imposing hardship on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly proclaim a policy of enlightened forbearance and decline further work on the grounds that it would overtax the people, all under Heaven would surely see Your Majesty as one who spares human labor and willingly burdens himself.

sentences.zh: 小臣固陋，不識忌諱，敢冒死上聞。

translations.literal: This petty official is indeed crude and ignorant, does not know taboos, and dares to risk death to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: I am but a humble and ignorant official, unversed in what may not be said, yet I dare risk my life to bring this before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 乞下臣此章，與執事者議其可否，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg that you transmit this memorial of mine to the responsible officials to discuss its advisability, then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that this memorial be forwarded to the responsible officials for deliberation on its merits, for then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，累轉起居舍人，兼知制誥，俄遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Shenlong he was successively transferred to diarist and concurrently charged with drafting edicts; soon he was promoted to secretary of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenlong he rose through successive posts to diarist and was concurrently charged with drafting edicts; soon he was promoted to secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 藏用常以俗多拘忌，有乖至理，乃著《析滯論》以暢其事，辭曰：客曰：“天道玄微，神理幽化，聖人所以法象，眾庶由其運行。

translations.literal: Zangyong often considered that popular custom was full of taboos contrary to ultimate principle; he therefore composed the "Discourse on Unblocking Stagnation" to set forth his views, saying: The Guest said: "The Way of Heaven is abstruse and subtle; the divine principle is darkly transformative—sages model themselves upon it, and the common multitude act according to its operations.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong often felt that popular custom was riddled with taboos at odds with ultimate principle, so he wrote the "Discourse on Unblocking Stagnation" to set forth his views. He wrote: The Guest said, "The Way of Heaven is abstruse and subtle, and the divine principle works in hidden transformation; sages take it as their model, and the common people live by its course.

sentences.zh: 故大撓造甲子，容成著律曆，黃公裁變，玄女啟謨，八門禦時，六神直事。

translations.literal: Therefore Da Rao created the sexagenary cycle, Rong Cheng authored the calendrical system, Huang Gong determined transformations, the Dark Lady opened the plan, the Eight Gates ward off the seasons, and the Six Spirits attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Da Rao devised the sexagenary cycle, Rong Cheng wrote the calendrical system, Huang Gong fixed the transformations, the Dark Lady revealed the design, the Eight Gates govern the seasons, and the Six Spirits oversee affairs.

sentences.zh: 從之者則兵強國富，違之者則將弱朝危，有同影響，若合符契。

translations.literal: Those who follow them have strong armies and wealthy states; those who violate them have weak generals and endangered courts—the effect is like shadow and echo, as if matching tally halves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow them grow strong in arms and rich in state; those who defy them find their generals weakened and their court endangered—the effect is immediate, like shadow and echo, as if tally halves were joined.

sentences.zh: 先生亦嚐聞之乎？”

translations.literal: Has the Master also heard of this?"
translations.idiomatic: Has the Master heard of this as well?"

sentences.zh: 主人曰：“何為其然也？

translations.literal: The Host said: "Why should this be so?
translations.idiomatic: The Host said, "Why should that be so?

sentences.zh: 子所謂曲學所習，需昧所守，徒識偏方之詭說，未究亨衢之通論。

translations.literal: What you speak of are cramped studies habitually learned and shallow convictions rigidly held—you merely know the eccentric claims of partial schools and have not investigated the comprehensive doctrine of the broad highway.
translations.idiomatic: What you describe are narrow studies learned by rote and dim convictions held blindly—you know only the eccentric claims of partial schools and have not examined the comprehensive doctrine of the open road.

sentences.zh: 蓋《易》曰“先天不違”，《傳》稱“人神之主”。

translations.literal: For the Changes says "He does not violate what precedes Heaven," and the Commentary calls it "the lord of man and spirit."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "He does not violate what precedes Heaven," and the Commentary calls it "the master of human and divine affairs."

sentences.zh: 範圍不過，三才所以虛中；

translations.literal: Its scope does not overstep, and therefore the three powers have emptiness at the center;
translations.idiomatic: Its scope does not overreach, and so the three powers hold emptiness at their center;

sentences.zh: 進退非邪，百王所以無外。

translations.literal: Its advance and retreat are without deviation, and therefore the hundred kings have nothing outside it.
translations.idiomatic: Its advance and retreat are without error, and so the hundred kings have nothing beyond it.

sentences.zh: 故曰：“國之將興聽於人，將亡聽於神。”

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "When a state is about to rise, heed people; when it is about to perish, heed spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying, "When a state is about to rise, listen to people; when it is about to fall, listen to spirits."

sentences.zh: 又曰：“禍福無門，唯人所召。

translations.literal: It is also said: "Fortune and misfortune have no gate of their own—only people summon them.
translations.idiomatic: And again, "Fortune and misfortune have no fixed gate—only people summon them.

sentences.zh: 人無釁焉，妖不自作。”

translations.literal: When people give no cause, portents do not arise of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When people give no cause, portents do not arise on their own."

sentences.zh: 由是言之，得喪興亡，並關人事；

translations.literal: From this it follows that gain and loss, rise and fall, all depend on human affairs;
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that gain and loss, rise and fall, all turn on human affairs;

sentences.zh: 吉凶悔吝，無涉天時。

translations.literal: good fortune, misfortune, regret, and distress have nothing to do with the timing of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: and good fortune, misfortune, regret, and distress have nothing to do with heavenly timing.

sentences.zh: 且皇天無親，唯德是輔，為不善者，天降之殃。

translations.literal: Moreover, High Heaven is without partiality and only assists virtue; for those who do what is not good, Heaven sends down calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, High Heaven is impartial and assists only virtue; for those who do wrong, Heaven sends down disaster.

sentences.zh: 高宗修德，桑穀以變；

translations.literal: When Gaozong cultivated virtue, the mulberry and grain transformed;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong cultivated virtue, the mulberry and grain changed of themselves;

sentences.zh: 宋君引過，法星退舍，此天道所以從人者也。

translations.literal: when the lord of Song acknowledged his fault, the Punishment Star withdrew from its lodge—this is how the Way of Heaven follows people.
translations.idiomatic: when the ruler of Song acknowledged his fault, the Punishment Star withdrew from its station—this is how the Way of Heaven follows human action.

sentences.zh: 古之為政者，刑獄不濫則人壽，賦斂蠲省則人富，法令有常則國靜，賞罰得中則兵強。

translations.literal: Ancient administrators of government—when punishments and prisons were not abused, people lived long; when levies and taxes were reduced and lightened, people grew wealthy; when laws and commands had constancy, the state was tranquil; when rewards and punishments were balanced, the army was strong.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers who governed well found that when punishments and prisons were not abused, people lived long; when levies and taxes were reduced, people grew wealthy; when laws and commands were steady, the state was calm; and when rewards and punishments were fair, the army was strong.

sentences.zh: 所以禮者，士之所歸，賞者，士之所死，禮賞不倦，則士爭先。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual is what gentlemen rally to, and rewards are what gentlemen die for—when ritual and reward never slacken, gentlemen vie to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is what gentlemen rally to, and reward is what they die for; when ritual and reward never flag, gentlemen compete to lead.

sentences.zh: 苟違此途，雖卜時行刑，擇日出令，必無成功矣。

translations.literal: If one departs from this course, even selecting times to execute punishment and choosing days to issue commands will surely bring no success.
translations.idiomatic: Depart from this path, and even if one chooses auspicious times to punish or issue orders, success is impossible.

sentences.zh: 自叔世遷訛，俗多徼幸，競稱怪力，爭誦詭言，屈政教而就孤虛，棄信賞而從推步。

translations.literal: From the later ages, as the times shifted into error, custom became full of hoping for luck; people competed to praise occult forces and vied to recite bizarre talk, bending government and education to submit to solitary-void divination, abandoning trust and rewards to follow calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Since later ages fell into error, custom has been full of hoping for lucky breaks; people compete to praise occult powers and recite strange doctrines, bending government and education to solitary-void divination and abandoning trust and reward for calendrical reckoning.

sentences.zh: 附會前史，變易舊經，依托空文，以為征據。

translations.literal: They forced links to past histories, altered old classics, relied on empty texts, and took these as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: They forced parallels with past histories, altered old classics, and treated empty texts as proof.

sentences.zh: 覆軍敗將者，則隱秘無聞；

translations.literal: When armies were destroyed and generals defeated, those cases were concealed and left unheard;
translations.idiomatic: When armies were destroyed and generals defeated, the cases were hushed up and never heard of;

sentences.zh: 偶同幸中者，則共相文飾。

translations.literal: when outcomes happened by chance to match, they embellished one another.
translations.idiomatic: when outcomes happened by lucky coincidence, they embellished one another.

sentences.zh: 豈唯德之增惑，亦乃學人自是。

translations.literal: Not only did this further confuse virtue—it also made scholars complacent in their own rightness.
translations.idiomatic: This not only further confused virtue; it also made scholars smug in their own opinions.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，習俗訛謬，一至此焉！

translations.literal: Alas, erroneous custom has reached this pitch!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, corrupt custom has reached this extreme!

sentences.zh: 昔者，甲子興師，非成功之日；

translations.literal: In the past, launching troops on a jiazi day was not a day for success;
translations.idiomatic: In the past, launching troops on a jiazi day was said to be no day for success;

sentences.zh: 往亡用事，異製勝之辰。

translations.literal: employing the Day of Past Dissolution differed from the hour for securing victory.
translations.idiomatic: and using the Day of Past Dissolution was unlike the moment for securing victory.

sentences.zh: 人事苟修，何往不濟？

translations.literal: If human affairs are properly cultivated, where would one go and not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: If human affairs are properly managed, where would one fail to succeed?

sentences.zh: 至若環城自守，接陣重圍，無闕地形，不乖天道。

translations.literal: As for encircling a city to hold it fast, or meeting the enemy in layered siege—terrain need not be lacking, and the Way of Heaven need not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Even when encircling a city in defense or facing layered sieges in battle, one need not lack favorable terrain or violate the Way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 若兵強將智，粟積城堅，雖復屢轉魁剛，頻移太歲，坐推白虎，行計貪狼，自符難鬥之祥，多貽蟻附之困。

translations.literal: If the army is strong and the general wise, grain is stocked and walls are sturdy—even if one repeatedly shifts the Kui and Gang stars, frequently moves the Year Star, sits calculating the White Tiger, and marches planning by the Greedy Wolf, naturally matching inauspicious signs for hard fighting, one mostly invites the trouble of ants clinging on.
translations.idiomatic: If the army is strong, the general wise, grain stocked, and walls solid, then even after repeatedly shifting the Kui and Gang stars, moving the Year Star, calculating the White Tiger while seated, and planning marches by the Greedy Wolf—matching every ill omen for hard fighting—one still mostly invites the plight of ants swarming a corpse.

sentences.zh: 故曰，任賢使能，則不時日而事利；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: employ the worthy and use the capable, and affairs prosper without heeding days and times;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: employ the worthy and use the capable, and affairs succeed without regard to days and times;

sentences.zh: 明法審令，則不卜筮而事吉；

translations.literal: clarify laws and examine commands, and affairs are auspicious without divination;
translations.idiomatic: clarify laws and examine commands, and affairs turn out well without divination;

sentences.zh: 養勞賞功，則不禱祠而得福。

translations.literal: nurture the weary and reward merit, and fortune is gained without prayer and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: care for the weary and reward merit, and blessing comes without prayer or sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 此所謂天時不如地利，地利不如人和。

translations.literal: This is what they call: the timing of Heaven is not as good as the advantage of terrain, and the advantage of terrain is not as good as human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by saying that heavenly timing is inferior to terrain, and terrain is inferior to human harmony.

sentences.zh: 太公犯雨，逆天時也，韓信背水，乖地利也，並存人事，俱成大業。

translations.literal: Taigong braved rain—going against the timing of Heaven; Han Xin fought with water at his back—contrary to terrain advantage; yet both relied on human affairs and alike achieved great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong marched in rain, defying heavenly timing; Han Xin fought with water at his back, contrary to terrain advantage—yet both relied on human affairs and alike achieved great success.

sentences.zh: 削樹而斬龐涓，舉火而屠張郃，未必暗同歲德，冥會日遊，俱運三門，並占四殺。

translations.literal: Felling trees to behead Pang Juan, raising fire to slaughter Zhang He—they need not secretly match the Year Virtue, secretly coincide with the Sun's circuit, jointly deploy the Three Gates, or together occupy the Four Kills.
translations.idiomatic: Felling trees to behead Pang Juan and raising fire to slaughter Zhang He did not require secretly matching the Year Virtue, secretly aligning with the Sun's circuit, jointly deploying the Three Gates, or together occupying the Four Kills.

sentences.zh: 杜郵齒劍，抑唯計沮，垓下悲歌，實階剚印。

translations.literal: At Duyang biting the sword—truly only Ji Ju schemed; the mournful song at Gaixia—in truth it was the step toward cutting the seal.
translations.idiomatic: The sword-biting at Duyang came down to Ji Ju's scheming alone; the mournful song at Gaixia was in truth the step toward having one's seal cut off.

sentences.zh: 若以並資厭勝，不事良圖，則長平盡坑，固須恒濟，襄城無噍，亦可常保。

translations.literal: If one relied equally on occult suppression and did not pursue sound planning, then the total slaughter at Changping would surely require the Eternal Ford, and the annihilation at Xiangcheng could also be permanently preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If one relied equally on occult suppression instead of sound planning, then the total slaughter at Changping would surely have needed the Eternal Ford, and the annihilation at Xiangcheng could also have been permanently avoided.

sentences.zh: 是知拘而多忌，終喪大功；

translations.literal: From this one knows that being constrained and full of taboos ultimately loses great achievement;
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that constraint and excessive taboos ultimately destroy great achievement;

sentences.zh: 百姓與能，必遺小數。

translations.literal: when the common people contribute their abilities, one must set aside petty reckonings.
translations.idiomatic: when the people contribute their abilities, one must leave petty reckonings aside.

sentences.zh: 金雞玉鶴，方為楚國之殃；

translations.literal: The golden rooster and jade crane proved to be the calamity of the state of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: The golden rooster and jade crane became the disaster of the state of Chu;

sentences.zh: 《萬畢》、《枕中》，適構淮南之禍。

translations.literal: The "Ten Thousand Completions" and "Pillow Book" just brought about the disaster of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Thousand Completions and Pillow Book brought about the disaster of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 刻符指盜，反更亡身；

translations.literal: Carving talismans to identify thieves yet instead brought about one's own death;
translations.idiomatic: Carving talismans to catch thieves instead brought about one's own death;

sentences.zh: 被髮邀神，翻招夷族。

translations.literal: Disheveling hair to invite spirits instead invited extermination of one's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Disheveling one's hair to summon spirits instead brought extermination upon one's clan.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，威鬥赭鞭，不禳赤伏之運；

translations.literal: Alas—the war-drum and ruddy whip could not avert the rise of the Red symbol;
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the war-drum and ruddy whip could not avert the rise of the Red symbol;

sentences.zh: 築城斷罔，何救素靈之哭！

translations.literal: Building walls and cutting dikes—how could they save the weeping of Su Ling!
translations.idiomatic: Building walls and cutting dikes—how could they save the weeping of Su Ling!

sentences.zh: 火災不驗，裨灶無力以窺天；

translations.literal: The fire disaster went unfulfilled, and Pixie Zao lacked strength to peer into Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The predicted fire disaster did not come to pass, and Pixie Zao lacked the power to read Heaven;

sentences.zh: 超乘階凶，王孫取監於觀德。

translations.literal: Leaping onto the chariot step brought misfortune—the king's grandson took warning from observing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Leaping onto the chariot step brought disaster; the king's grandson took his lesson from observing virtue.

sentences.zh: 九征九變，是曰長途；

translations.literal: Nine probes and nine transformations—this is called the long journey;
translations.idiomatic: Nine probes and nine transformations—this is called the long road;

sentences.zh: 人謀鬼謀，良歸有道。

translations.literal: Human planning and ghostly planning alike ultimately return to the proper Way.
translations.idiomatic: Human planning and ghostly planning alike ultimately return to the proper Way.

sentences.zh: 此並經史陳跡，賢聖通規，仁遠乎哉，詎宜滯執？”

translations.literal: These are all tracks laid out in the classics and histories, the universal norms of the sage and worthy—is humanity far away? How could one cling rigidly?"
translations.idiomatic: These are all precedents set forth in the classics and histories, the universal norms of sages and worthies—is humanity really so far away? Why cling so rigidly?"

sentences.zh: 客乃蹙然避席曰：“鄙人困蒙，不階至道，請事斯語，歸於正途。

translations.literal: The Guest then, looking abashed, withdrew from his mat and said: "This rustic is benumbed and ignorant, not having reached the supreme Way—allow me to take these words and return to the proper path.
translations.idiomatic: The Guest then, abashed, withdrew from his mat and said, "I am a dull and ignorant man who has not reached the supreme Way. Allow me to follow these words and return to the proper path.

sentences.zh: 而今而後，焚蓍龜，毀律曆，廢六合，斥五行，浩然清慮，則將奚若？”

translations.literal: From now on, burning the yarrow and tortoise, destroying calendars, abolishing the six harmonies, rejecting the five phases, with vast clear-mindedness—what then shall I be like?"
translations.idiomatic: From now on, if I burn the yarrow and tortoise, destroy calendars, abolish the six harmonies, and reject the five phases, and with vast clarity of mind—what then shall I become?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：“此所謂過猶不及也。

translations.literal: The reply said: "This is what they call going too far is as bad as not going far enough.
translations.idiomatic: The reply said, "This is what is meant by going too far is no better than falling short.

sentences.zh: 夫甲子所以配日月，律曆所以通歲時，金木所以備法象，蓍龜所以筮吉凶。

translations.literal: The sexagenary cycle matches sun and moon; calendars connect with the seasons; metal and wood complete the modeled images; yarrow and tortoise divination determine fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The sexagenary cycle matches sun and moon; calendars align with the seasons; metal and wood complete the modeled images; yarrow and tortoise are used to divine fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 聖人以此神明德行，輔助謀猷，存之則協讚成功，執之則凝滯於物。

translations.literal: The sage uses these to illuminate virtue and conduct and assist in deliberation—preserved, they harmoniously help success; rigidly held, they stagnate and bind one to things.
translations.idiomatic: Sages use these to illuminate virtue and conduct and to assist deliberation; kept in their place, they harmoniously aid success; clung to rigidly, they freeze one in attachment to things.

sentences.zh: 消息之義，其在茲乎！”

translations.literal: The meaning of waxing and waning—is it not here!"
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of waxing and waning—is it not found here!"

sentences.zh: 客於是循牆匍匐，帖然無氣，口去心醉，不知所以答矣。

translations.literal: The Guest then crawled along the wall in prostration, utterly subdued and breathless, mouth agape and heart intoxicated, not knowing how to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Guest then crawled along the wall in prostration, utterly subdued and breathless, mouth agape and heart overwhelmed, not knowing how to answer.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Jinglong he served as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong he served as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 藏用性無挺特，多為權要所逼，頗隳公道。

translations.literal: Zangyong's nature lacked firm uprightness; he was often pressed by powerful figures and considerably undermined public justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong's nature lacked firm uprightness; he was often pressed by powerful figures and considerably undermined public justice.

sentences.zh: 又遷黃門侍郎，兼昭文館學士，轉工部侍郎、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was further transferred to secretary of the Yellow Gate and concurrently made a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall, then transferred to vice minister of works and right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was further transferred to secretary of the Yellow Gate and concurrently made a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall, then transferred to vice minister of works and right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 先天中，坐托附太平公主，配流嶺表。

translations.literal: During Xiantian, for relying on Princess Taiping, he was sentenced to exile in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiantian, for relying on Princess Taiping, he was sentenced to exile in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 開元初，起為黔州都督府長史，兼判都督事，未行而卒，年五十餘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was recalled as chief administrator of the Qianzhou metropolitan prefecture and concurrently judged metropolitan affairs, but died before taking up the post, at age fifty-some.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was recalled as chief administrator of the Qianzhou metropolitan prefecture and concurrently judged metropolitan affairs, but died before taking up the post at the age of fifty-some.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 藏用工篆隸，好琴棋，當時稱為多能之士。

translations.literal: Zangyong was skilled in seal and clerical script and fond of zither and chess; he was called a man of many talents in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong was skilled in seal and clerical script and fond of zither and chess; he was called a man of many talents in his day.

sentences.zh: 少與陳子昂、趙貞固友善，二人並早卒，藏用厚撫其子，為時所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was close friends with Chen Zi'ang and Zhao Zhengu; both died early, and Zangyong generously supported their sons, for which he was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close friends with Chen Zi'ang and Zhao Zhengu; both died early, and Zangyong generously supported their sons, for which he was praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 然初隱居之時，有貞儉之操，往來於少室、終南二山，時人稱為“隨駕隱士”；

translations.literal: Yet when he first retired from the world he had a character of integrity and frugality, traveling between Mount Shaoshi and Mount Zhongnan; people of the time called him "the hermit who follows the imperial carriage";
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he first retired from the world he had a character of integrity and frugality, traveling between Mount Shaoshi and Mount Zhongnan; people of the day called him "the hermit who follows the imperial carriage";

sentences.zh: 及登朝，趑趄詭佞，專事權貴，奢靡淫縱，以此獲譏於世。

translations.literal: once he entered court service he fawned and flattered, devoted himself to the powerful, and lived in extravagance and dissipation—for this he was ridiculed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: once he entered court service he fawned and flattered, devoted himself to the powerful, and lived in extravagance and dissipation—for this he was ridiculed by the world.

sentences.zh: 徐彥伯

translations.literal: Xu Yanbo
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanbo

sentences.zh: 徐彥伯，兗州瑕丘人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yanbo was a native of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanbo came from Xiaqiu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以文章擅名，河北道安撫大使薛元超表薦之，對策擢第，累轉蒲州司兵參軍。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for his essays; Xue Yuanchao, commissioner for pacification of the Hebei circuit, memorialized recommending him; he passed the policy examination and through successive appointments became military recorder of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was famed for his essays; Xue Yuanchao, commissioner for pacification of the Hebei circuit, memorialized recommending him; he passed the policy examination and rose through successive posts to military recorder of Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時司戶韋暠善判事，司士李亙工於翰劄，而彥伯以文辭雅美，時人謂之“河中三絕”。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Hao of the revenue section was skilled at adjudication, Li Gen of the labor section was adept at letters, and Yanbo was elegant in literary composition; people of the time called them "the three unmatched talents of Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Hao of the revenue section was skilled at adjudication, Li Gen of the labor section was adept at letters, and Yanbo was elegant in literary composition; people of the day called them "the three unmatched talents of Hedong."

sentences.zh: 彥伯聖曆中累除給事中，時王公卿士多以言語不慎，密為酷吏周興、來俊臣等所陷，彥伯乃著《樞機論》以誡於代，其辭曰：

translations.literal: During Shenli Yanbo was successively appointed gentleman-attendant; at that time many princes, dukes, and officials were secretly framed by cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen for careless speech; Yanbo therefore composed the "Discourse on the Pivot of Power" to warn the generation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: During Shenli Yanbo was successively appointed gentleman-attendant; at that time many princes, dukes, and officials were secretly framed by cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen for careless speech; Yanbo therefore composed the "Discourse on the Pivot of Power" to warn his generation, saying:

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：“唯口起羞，惟甲胃起戎。”

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says, "It is the mouth that gives rise to disgrace; it is armor and helmet that give rise to warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "It is the mouth that gives rise to disgrace; it is armor and helmet that give rise to warfare."

sentences.zh: 又云：“齊乃位，度乃口。”

translations.literal: It also says, "Make yourself correct, and measure your words."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Make yourself upright, and measure your words."

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：“慎言語，節飲食。”

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "Be careful in speech; moderate food and drink."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Be careful in speech and moderate in food and drink."

sentences.zh: 又云：“出其言善，千里應之；

translations.literal: It also says, "When what one puts forth is good, it is answered from a thousand li away;
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "When what one puts forth is good, it is answered from a thousand li away;

sentences.zh: 出其言不善，千里違之。”

translations.literal: when what one puts forth is not good, it is opposed from a thousand li away."
translations.idiomatic: when what one puts forth is not good, it is opposed from a thousand li away."

sentences.zh: 《禮》亦云：“可言也，不可行也，君子不言也；

translations.literal: The Book of Rites also says, "What may be said but cannot be done—the gentleman does not say it;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites also says, "What may be said but cannot be done, the gentleman does not say it;

sentences.zh: 可行也，不可言也，君子不行也。”

translations.literal: what may be done but cannot be said—the gentleman does not do it."
translations.idiomatic: what may be done but cannot be said, the gentleman does not do it."

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 先聖知言之為大也，知言之為急也，精微以勸之，典謨以告之，禮經以防之。

translations.literal: The ancient sages knew how great a matter speech is, knew how urgent a matter speech is—they exhorted with subtle principles, instructed with canonical models, and guarded against it with the Classic of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sages knew how great a matter speech is and how urgent a matter it is. They exhorted with subtle principles, instructed with canonical models, and guarded against its dangers with the Classic of Rites.

sentences.zh: 守名教者，何可不修其詁訓而服其糟粕乎？

translations.literal: Those who uphold orthodox teaching—how can they fail to study its glosses and commentaries and submit to its essential leavings?
translations.idiomatic: Those who uphold orthodox teaching—how can they fail to study its glosses and commentaries and live by its distilled precepts?

sentences.zh: 故曰：“言語者，君子之樞機，動則物應，物應則得失之兆見也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, "Speech is the pivot and trigger of the gentleman—when it moves, things respond; when things respond, the auguries of gain and loss appear.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said, "Speech is the pivot and trigger of the gentleman. When it moves, things respond; when things respond, the signs of gain and loss appear.

sentences.zh: 得之者江海比鄰，失之者肝膽楚、越，然後知否泰榮辱，係於言乎！

translations.literal: Those who succeed in it find neighbors across rivers and seas; those who fail find heart and liver separated like Chu and Yue—and only then does one know whether prosperity and decline, glory and disgrace, depend upon speech!
translations.idiomatic: Those who succeed in it find neighbors as close as those across rivers and seas; those who fail find heart and liver torn apart like Chu and Yue. Only then does one know that prosperity and decline, glory and disgrace, depend upon speech!

sentences.zh: 夫言者，德之柄也，行之主也，誌之端也，身之文也，既可以濟身，亦可以覆身。

translations.literal: Speech is the handle of virtue, the master of conduct, the beginning of intent, the ornament of the person—it can both save the person and can also destroy the person.
translations.idiomatic: Speech is the handle of virtue, the master of conduct, the beginning of intent, and the ornament of the person. It can both save a person and destroy a person.

sentences.zh: 故中庸鏤其心，右階銘其背，南容復於白圭，箕子疇於《洪範》，良有以也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Doctrine of the Mean was engraved upon the heart, the right-hand steps bore inscriptions on the back, Nan Rong repeated the white-jade maxim, and Jizi set forth the Great Plan—there was good reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Doctrine of the Mean was engraved upon the heart, moral maxims were inscribed on the right-hand steps and upon the back, Nan Rong repeated the white-jade maxim, and Jizi set forth the Great Plan—all for good reason.

sentences.zh: 是以掎摭瑕玷，參詳躁競，審無常以階亂，將不密以致危。

translations.literal: Therefore one must gather and inspect every flaw, weigh anxious contention carefully, recognize that inconstancy paves the way to disorder, and recognize that lack of secrecy leads to danger.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one must gather and inspect every flaw, weigh anxious contention carefully, recognize that inconstancy paves the way to disorder, and recognize that lack of discretion leads to danger.

sentences.zh: 利生於口，森然覆邦之說；

translations.literal: Profit arising from the mouth—there is talk dense enough to overturn the state;
translations.idiomatic: Profit arising from the mouth—there is talk dense enough to overturn a state;

sentences.zh: 道不由衷，變彼如簧之刺。

translations.literal: the Way not proceeding from the heart—how it transforms into those reed-pipe barbs!
translations.idiomatic: when the Way does not proceed from the heart, it turns into those slanderous barbs like reed pipes!

sentences.zh: 可不懼之哉！

translations.literal: Should one not fear this!
translations.idiomatic: Should one not fear this!

sentences.zh: 其有識暗邪正，慮微形朕，破金湯之龠，封禍亂之根，用詀讘為全計，以號詉為令德。

translations.literal: There are those who fail to discern right from wrong, who detect the faintest marks, break through gates of bronze and moats of iron, seal up the roots of calamity and disorder, employ revilement as a complete stratagem, and take shouting abuse as excellent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: There are those who fail to discern right from wrong, who detect the faintest signs of offense, break through gates of bronze and moats of iron, seal up the roots of calamity and disorder, employ revilement as a complete stratagem, and treat shouting abuse as excellent virtue.

sentences.zh: 至若梧宮問答，荊、齊所以奔命；

translations.literal: For instance, the question-and-answer at the Wu Palace—therefore Jing and Qi raced to answer the call;
translations.idiomatic: Consider, for instance, the question-and-answer at the Wu Palace, which set Jing and Qi racing to answer the call;

sentences.zh: 韓、魏加肘，智伯所以危殘。

translations.literal: when Han and Wei applied the elbow hold—therefore Zhi Bo was endangered and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: when Han and Wei applied the elbow hold, Zhi Bo was endangered and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 蔡侯繩息媯也，亟招甲兵之罰；

translations.literal: Duke Ai of Cai tied up Xi Gui—and quickly brought upon himself the punishment of armored troops;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai of Cai tied up Xi Gui and quickly brought upon himself the punishment of armored troops;

sentences.zh: 鄭曼圖宗卿也，而受鼎鑊之誅。

translations.literal: Zheng Man plotted against the minister of the ancestral temple—and received execution by cauldron and boiling.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Man plotted against the minister of the ancestral temple and received execution by cauldron and boiling.

sentences.zh: 史遷輕議，終下蠶室；

translations.literal: Sima Qian lightly criticized—and in the end descended to the Silkworm Chamber;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian spoke lightly in criticism and in the end was sent down to the Silkworm Chamber;

sentences.zh: 張紘說，更齒龍淵。

translations.literal: Zhang Hong's persuasion—again teeth at Dragon Abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong's persuasion again cost teeth at Dragon Abyss.

sentences.zh: 凡此過言，其流匪一。

translations.literal: All such excessive speech—its currents are not one.
translations.idiomatic: All such excessive speech—its currents are not one.

sentences.zh: 或穢猶糞土，或動成刀劍，或苟且其心，或脂膏其吻。

translations.literal: Some vile as dung and soil, some the moment they move become swords and blades; some debased in mind, some with lips grease-slicked.
translations.idiomatic: Some are vile as dung and soil; some the moment they move become swords and blades; some are debased in mind; some grease their lips with flattery.

sentences.zh: 挾邪作蠱，守之而不懈；

translations.literal: Wielding depravity and working witchcraft, they hold to it without slackening;
translations.idiomatic: Wielding depravity and working witchcraft, they hold to it without slackening;

sentences.zh: 往輒破的，去之而彌遠。

translations.literal: going forth they always pierce the target; departing from it they go ever farther.
translations.idiomatic: going forth they always hit the mark; turning from it they go ever farther astray.

sentences.zh: 亦可異韓廬聚音，釐也群吠，得死為幸，何循名之立乎？

translations.literal: How strange—like Han Lu gathering voices and Li howling in a pack: to die by chance would be fortune—how can upright reputation be established?
translations.idiomatic: How strange—like Han Lu gathering voices and Li howling in a pack: to die by chance would be good fortune. How then can an upright reputation be established?

sentences.zh: 雖復伯玉沮顏，追謝於元凱，蔣濟貽恨，失譽於王陵，犀首沒齒於季章，曹瞞齚舌於劉主，當何及哉！

translations.literal: Even if Qu Boyu looked ashamed and later apologized to Yuan Kai; even if Jiang Ji left behind regret and lost reputation before Wang Ling; even if Xi Shou lost his teeth before Ji Zhang; even if Cao Man clenched his tongue before Lord Liu—what good would it come to!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Qu Boyu looked ashamed and later apologized to Yuan Kai; even if Jiang Ji left behind regret and lost his reputation before Wang Ling; even if Xi Shou lost his teeth before Ji Zhang; even if Cao Man clenched his tongue before Lord Liu—what good would it do!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：“予欲無言。”

translations.literal: Confucius said, "I wish to speak no more."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "I wish to speak no more."

sentences.zh: 又云：“終身為善一言敗之，惜也。”

translations.literal: He also said, "To do good all one's life and have one word ruin it—how regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "To do good all one's life and have one word ruin it—how regrettable."

sentences.zh: 老子亦云：“多言數窮。”

translations.literal: Laozi also said, "Much speaking ends in exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi also said, "Much speaking ends in exhaustion."

sentences.zh: 又雲“聰明深察而近於死者，議人者也。”

translations.literal: He also said, "Those who are clever and deeply observant and yet approach death—such are those who discuss others."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Those who are clever and deeply observant and yet approach death are those who discuss others."

sentences.zh: 何聖人之深思偉慮，杜漸防萌之至乎！

translations.literal: How deeply the sages thought, how grandly they considered—to the utmost of stopping what is beginning and guarding against what is sprouting!
translations.idiomatic: How deeply the sages thought and how grandly they considered—to the utmost of stopping what is beginning and guarding against what is sprouting!

sentences.zh: 夫不可言而言者曰狂，可言而不言者曰隱。

translations.literal: What must not be spoken yet is spoken is called reckless; what may be spoken yet is not spoken is called secretive.
translations.idiomatic: What must not be spoken yet is spoken is called reckless; what may be spoken yet is not spoken is called secretive.

sentences.zh: 鉗舌拱默，曷通彼此之懷；

translations.literal: Clamping the tongue and bowing in silence—how can the feelings of both parties be communicated;
translations.idiomatic: Clamping the tongue and bowing in silence—how can the feelings of both parties be communicated;

sentences.zh: 括囊而處，孰啟謨明之訓？

translations.literal: pocketing the mouth and dwelling thus—who will open the instruction of counsel and clarity?
translations.idiomatic: pocketing the mouth and dwelling thus—who will open the instruction of counsel and clarity?

sentences.zh: 則上言者，下聽也；

translations.literal: Then what the superior speaks—the subordinate listens to;
translations.idiomatic: Then what the superior speaks, the subordinate listens to;

sentences.zh: 下言者，上用也。

translations.literal: what the subordinate speaks—the superior employs.
translations.idiomatic: what the subordinate speaks, the superior employs.

sentences.zh: 睿哲之言，猶天地也，人覆燾而生焉；

translations.literal: Words of sage wisdom are like Heaven and Earth—people live covered beneath their nurturing canopy;
translations.idiomatic: Words of sage wisdom are like Heaven and Earth—people live beneath their nurturing canopy;

sentences.zh: 大雅之言，猶鍾鼓也，人考擊而樂焉。

translations.literal: Words of great elegance are like bells and drums—people find joy in striking and sounding them.
translations.idiomatic: Words of great elegance are like bells and drums—people find joy in striking and sounding them.

sentences.zh: 作以龜鏡，姬公之言也；

translations.literal: Made as a mirror of tortoise shell—such were the words of the Duke of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Made as a mirror of tortoise shell—such were the words of the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 出為金石，曾子之言也；

translations.literal: Coming forth as metal and stone—such were the words of Zengzi;
translations.idiomatic: Coming forth as metal and stone—such were the words of Zengzi;

sentences.zh: 存其家邦，國僑之言也；

translations.literal: Preserving his house and state—such were the words of Zichan;
translations.idiomatic: Preserving his house and state—such were the words of Zichan;

sentences.zh: 立而不朽，臧孫之言也。

translations.literal: Standing without decay—such were the words of Zang Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Standing without decay—such were the words of Zang Sun.

sentences.zh: 是謂德音，詣我宗極，滿於天下，貽厥後昆。

translations.literal: These are called virtuous words—reaching our ancestral apex, filling all under Heaven, bequeathing to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: These are called virtuous words—reaching our ancestral apex, filling all under Heaven, and bequeathing to posterity.

sentences.zh: 殷宗甘之於酒醴，孫卿諭之以琴瑟，闕里重於四時，郢都輕其千乘。

translations.literal: The Yin dynast lord sweetly took to wine and spirits; Sun Qing admonished him with lute and zither; Queli was heavier than the four seasons; Ying capital lightly held its thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin dynast lord sweetly indulged in wine and spirits; Sun Qing admonished him with lute and zither; Queli was valued more than the four seasons; Ying capital lightly held its thousand chariots.

sentences.zh: 豈不韙哉，豈不休哉！

translations.literal: Is this not correct! Is this not glorious!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not correct! Is this not glorious!

sentences.zh: 但楙探世猷，克念丕訓，審思而應，精慮而動。

translations.literal: But one should deeply probe the ways of the world, earnestly recall the great instruction, respond only after careful thought, and act only after refined deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: But one should deeply probe the ways of the world, earnestly hold in mind the great instruction, respond only after careful thought, and act only after refined deliberation.

sentences.zh: 謀其心以後發，擇其交以後談，不蹙趨於非黨，不屏營於詭遇。

translations.literal: Plan in the heart before speaking, choose one's company before talking; do not press hurriedly toward hostile factions, do not hide and scheme for deceptive encounters.
translations.idiomatic: Plan in the heart before speaking and choose one's company before talking. Do not press hurriedly toward hostile factions, and do not hide and scheme for deceptive encounters.

sentences.zh: 非先王之至德不敢行，非先王之法言不敢道，翦其諜諜之緒，撲其炎炎之勢。

translations.literal: Without the utmost virtue of the former kings one dares not act; without the model words of the former kings one dares not speak—cut off the trailing threads of whispered scheming, beat down the blazing momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Without the utmost virtue of the former kings one dares not act; without the model words of the former kings one dares not speak. Cut off the trailing threads of whispered scheming and beat down the blazing momentum.

sentences.zh: 自然介爾景福，錫茲純嘏，則悔吝何由而生，怨惡何由而至哉？

translations.literal: Naturally the great blessing will come to you, and this pure felicity will be granted—then from what would regret and distress arise, from what would resentment and hatred come?
translations.idiomatic: Naturally the great blessing will come to you and this pure felicity will be granted—then from what would regret and distress arise, and from what would resentment and hatred come?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：“終日行，不遺已患；

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Going all day without forgetting oneself brings no calamity;"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Going all day without forgetting oneself brings no calamity;"

sentences.zh: 終日言，不遺已憂。”

translations.literal: speaking all day without forgetting oneself brings no worry."
translations.idiomatic: speaking all day without forgetting oneself brings no worry."

sentences.zh: 如此乃可以言也。

translations.literal: Only thus may one speak.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus may one speak.

sentences.zh: 戒之哉，戒之哉！”

translations.literal: Be on guard! Be on guard!"
translations.idiomatic: Be on guard! Be on guard!"

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，遷太常少卿，兼修國史，以預修《則天實錄》成，封高平縣子，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently charged with compiling the national history; for his participation in completing the Veritable Records of Wu Zetian he was enfeoffed as viscount of Gaoping County and granted five hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently charged with compiling the national history; for his participation in completing the Veritable Records of Wu Zetian he was enfeoffed as viscount of Gaoping County and granted five hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為衛州刺史，以善政聞，璽書勞勉。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Wei Prefecture; he was famed for good governance and was commended in an imperial letter with the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Wei Prefecture; he was famed for good governance and was commended in an imperial letter with the seal.

sentences.zh: 俄轉蒲州刺史，入為工部侍郎，尋除衛尉卿，兼昭文館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Pu Prefecture, entered court as vice minister of works, and soon was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Stud and concurrently made a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Pu Prefecture, entered court as vice minister of works, and soon was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Stud and concurrently made a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，中宗親拜南郊，彥伯作《南郊賦》以獻，辭甚典美。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong Zhongzong personally performed the southern suburban sacrifice; Yanbo composed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb" and presented it—the language was very classical and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jinglong Zhongzong personally performed the southern suburban sacrifice; Yanbo composed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb" and presented it—the language was very classical and elegant.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，加銀青光祿大夫，遷右散騎常侍、太子賓客，仍兼昭文館學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun he was given the silver-blue-golden grand master of the palace and transferred to right attendant cavalier and guest of the crown prince, still concurrently a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingyun he was given the silver-blue-golden grand master of the palace and transferred to right attendant cavalier and guest of the crown prince, still concurrently a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，以疾乞骸骨，許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian, on account of illness he requested to retire; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian, on account of illness he requested to retire; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 開元二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 彥伯事寡嫂甚謹，撫諸侄同於己子。

translations.literal: Yanbo served his widowed sister-in-law with great respect and raised his nephews as he did his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo served his widowed sister-in-law with great respect and raised his nephews as he did his own sons.

sentences.zh: 自晚年屬文，好為強澀之體，頗為後進所效焉。

translations.literal: From his later years in composing essays he favored a forceful and abstruse style, which many younger writers imitated.
translations.idiomatic: From his later years in composing essays he favored a forceful and abstruse style, which many younger writers imitated.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷，行於時。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to twenty juan and circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan and circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: The Historian's Comment
translations.idiomatic: The Historian's Comment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：才出於智，行出於性。

translations.literal: The historian says: Talent comes from intelligence; conduct comes from nature.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Talent comes from intelligence; conduct comes from nature.

sentences.zh: 故文章巧拙，由智之深淺也；

translations.literal: Thus whether essays are skillful or clumsy depends on the depth or shallowness of intelligence;
translations.idiomatic: Thus whether essays are skillful or clumsy depends on the depth or shallowness of intelligence;

sentences.zh: 行義詭實，由性之善惡也。

translations.literal: whether conduct is upright or devious, genuine or false, depends on the goodness or wickedness of nature.
translations.idiomatic: whether conduct is upright or devious, genuine or false, depends on the goodness or wickedness of nature.

sentences.zh: 然則智性稟之於氣，不可使之強也。

translations.literal: Intelligence and nature are endowed by vital force and cannot be forced to grow stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence and nature are endowed by vital force and cannot be forced to grow stronger.

sentences.zh: 蘇味道、李嶠等，俱為輔相，各處穹崇。

translations.literal: Su Weidao, Li Jiao, and the like all served as chief ministers, each occupying the highest eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao, Li Jiao, and the like all served as chief ministers, each occupying the highest eminence.

sentences.zh: 觀其章疏之能，非無奧贍；

translations.literal: Judging their ability in memorials and reports, they were not without depth and richness;
translations.idiomatic: Judging their ability in memorials and reports, they were not without depth and richness;

sentences.zh: 驗以弼諧之道，罔有貞純。

translations.literal: yet tested by the way of assisting and harmonizing, they had no steadfast integrity.
translations.idiomatic: yet tested by the way of assisting and harmonizing, they had no steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 故狄仁傑有言曰：“蘇、李足為文吏矣。”

translations.literal: Therefore Di Renjie had a saying: "Su and Li are sufficient as literary officials."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Di Renjie had a saying: "Su and Li are sufficient as literary officials."

sentences.zh: 得非齷齪者乎！

translations.literal: Were they not petty and narrow-minded men!
translations.idiomatic: Were they not petty and narrow-minded men!

sentences.zh: 模棱之病，尤足可譏。

translations.literal: The disease of equivocation especially deserves ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: The disease of equivocation especially deserves ridicule.

sentences.zh: 崔融、盧藏用、徐彥伯等，文學之功，不讓蘇、李，知有守常之道，而無應變之機。

translations.literal: Cui Rong, Lu Zangyong, Xu Yanbo, and the like did not yield to Su and Li in literary achievement; they knew the way of holding to constancy but lacked the resourcefulness to meet change.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong, Lu Zangyong, Xu Yanbo, and the like did not yield to Su and Li in literary achievement; they knew the way of holding to constancy but lacked the resourcefulness to meet change.

sentences.zh: 規諫之深，崔比盧、徐，稍為優矣。

translations.literal: In the depth of remonstrance Cui compared with Lu and Xu was somewhat superior.
translations.idiomatic: In the depth of remonstrance Cui compared with Lu and Xu was somewhat superior.

sentences.zh: 贊

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 贊曰：房、杜、姚、宋，俱立大功。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Fang, Du, Yao, and Song all established great merit.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Fang, Du, Yao, and Song all established great merit.

sentences.zh: 鹹以二族，譚為美風。

translations.literal: All praised these two pairs as models of fine conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All praised these two pairs as models of fine conduct.

sentences.zh: 蘇、李文學，一代之雄。

translations.literal: Su and Li in literary learning were heroes of their generation.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Li in literary learning were heroes of their generation.

sentences.zh: 有慚輔弼，稱之豈同。

translations.literal: Yet as chief ministers they were shamed; to call them the same is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as chief ministers they fell short; to call them the same is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 凡人有言，未必有德。

translations.literal: All men may have words, but not necessarily virtue.
translations.idiomatic: All men may have words, but not necessarily virtue.

sentences.zh: 崔與盧、徐，皆攻翰墨。

translations.literal: Cui and Lu and Xu all devoted themselves to brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Lu, and Xu all devoted themselves to brush and ink.

sentences.zh: 文雖堪尚，義無可則。

translations.literal: Their writing may be admired, but in righteousness there is nothing to take as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Their writing may be admired, but in righteousness there is nothing to take as a model.

sentences.zh: 備位守常，斯言罔忒。

translations.literal: Holding office and keeping to constancy—this saying is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Holding office and keeping to constancy—this saying is not wrong.
